question to one of the main theorist of the game who is your favorite character or characters? in no order I for some reason always wanted to ask moonflare that question,if for some reason I had ask it before, my memory is shit
Click to expand...
That is such a hard question given the intro to it. I'll start by listing some characters that are good places to spark theories from:
Well, in terms of theorizing, I guess I'd have to say Yasu. Even replaying for the third time, it's hard to properly identify what she's talking about sometimes.
One could probably also say Ami, given recent revelations and how we'll now always be on the lookout for her to out herself since the start of the game. But those are more of generic answers in terms of how much could be theorized from them.
I guess Nodoka could apply until recently, but we pretty much know most secrets about her at this point. There's some backstory, but we have enough to understand almost everything she did during the course of the game.
As for myself, I am and always will be drawn to Maya (Prime) and Himawari personally. And I'll put the both of them together because I kind of love them for the same reason.



I mean, Maya's the big mystery by design. And Himawari is the daughter from the future trying to stealthly change the variable that corrects everything.

How can they not be my favorites? Although I do make the distinction between Maya and Maya Prime because what draws me to Maya is more the denpa aspect of it (thousand year old tragic heroine that doesn't give up on her one true love), and how she's very loosely an Okabe to Akira's Kurisu (Steins;Gate).
And if I totally didn't understand the question, these are just favorite characters without any relevant theorizing:
I'd say that I love Rin because she reminds me of myself as a teenager, and because of the wholesome relationship with Akira.
I also love Sara for how realistic she feels to me.
And Yuki for owning up to her mistakes like a teacher with one last lesson to teach.
And lastly, in terms of romance, I just want Yumi to be happy.
So yeah, my top picks are:

Tier 1: Maya and Himawari (for being what the game is about, to me).
Tier 2: Rin (for being a wholesome disaster), Sara (for being real), Yuki (for teaching me something), Yumi (because I want her to be happy).

I'd also like to forward the question to the rest of the thread, which are your favorite characters and why?

This ♫ reminded me ♫ of something that blasted me upside the head the other day, curious about everyone's take here...

I think the concept of a "Reset" was born the same place so many of our misconceptions were born; Maya making assumptions in obsessive, love-blind desperation. I think a Reset is actually the collapse of a timeline and something about Akira is (was?) helping a few people slip with him into a new one. The true limitations and mechanics are obviously hard to pin down, but I think the ramblings of Yasu, the Gods and scenes like this one are telling us enough to see one of the foundational elements:


Chapter 4 Generic: Afternoon Library

-----

I think that Akira's state of mind and cognition play a heavy role in what kind of timeline people slip to, with others (including the Gods) have less of an impact. Was the chaotic slipping in our most recent "Reset" due to Pareidolia (and/or lack thereof), the empty wishing well or the fact that Akira's just lost as fuck trying to decide what to do about the loss of Maya?

Should he move on and find happiness in Ami's happiness-

Chapter 4 Main: Recap

-even though she would forsake the world just to keep him to herself?

Chapter 4 Main: Pop Goes the Weasel


...Try to embrace Nu Maya-

Chapter 4 Maya: The Girl Who Leapt Through Time

-despite wanting nothing more than to keep her as far away as possible?

Chapter 4 Maya: Right as Rain


...Or believe in the love of the one soul that would dive into the sun to put a smile on his face-

Chapter 4 Ayane: Time, Resets and the Like

-and continue fighting to recover the one he would drown in?

Chapter 4 Main: Episcopalis: A Hymn for Him and She and Her

-----

To me, there always seems to be this struggle in four directions:

1. The world is made for Akira.
2. The world is made for the Player.
3. The world is made by god(s) and they're using Akira and Kumon-Mi for their own purposes.
4. The world is ambivalent to all of this and each individuals' pain and joy are the only thing that's truly real.

And I feel like I have no choice but to conclude that this work is trying to allow the narrative to acknowledge and develop the fact that ALL of these things are true at the same time.

The way I like to think of it right now is something like this (preface that this is all just for fun and not an attempt to solve a puzzle for good):

1. The world is made for the developer (God)
2. The developer cannot enter the world, however, as it is fiction.
3. The developer chooses Akira to go in for him because Akira is an empty husk and therefore ideal for placing oneself into.
3.5. The bulk of narration/dialogue we see from Akira is from the Developer.
4. The player is allowed auxiliary control over Akira for reasons I am uncertain about.
5. "The world" is everything that is the case; the limits of the Developer's language are the limits of the world.

Which coalesces into something like:
Akira stands at the edge of a school building and prepares to jump off. In this moment he gives up individual agency and God allows the player to control Akira. We tell him to jump. He does. posts.content_html_raw:
Moonflare said:
I'd also like to forward the question to the rest of the thread, which are your favorite characters and why?
Click to expand...
These are always hard for me since I don't think I'm good at explaining my feelings about each girl and I can never rank them after a few. It then comes down to do I like/love them or do I want zero events with them present.

Maya/Niki
They have always been tied in my brain and that's just the way it is for me. They are both the best.

I just connected with Maya right from the start way more than I did Ami. I want to say I suspected right away she had some connection with Sensei and I could feel a sadness or something like that in her but I'm probably full of shit and just liked her look. I know I've always loved her hair and eyes (and her smiles are precious). Like you said with Yumi (and I agree) I just want Maya to be happy. I have felt close to her since the very beginning of the game and its only gotten stronger. I think New Maya might be growing on me, that talk last update helped me out as well as them. You could argue she beats Niki because I could listen to Good Morning over and over and the reason I love it is because of the association to Maya.

As for Niki, she can be a loud, bitchy, and very pushy person but there is also something about her that I loved from her first appearance. It cant be just the pink hair because I don't feel the same about Noriko. Like Maya I feel that she loves Akira very much and to me its a truer(?) love than many of the other girls. I don't know, very hard to explain, could just be nothing more than I like her. Could be the letters that did it. Could be that very emotional event chain I forget the name of.

Ayane
I don't remember liking her much at the start but as the game went on and she showed how great a person she was and how much she stuck by Akira I just started to like her more and more. I think she is fantastic now and I want her to be a part of every ending with him.

Sara (probably)
The rest of my favorites kinda meld together and bounce around but I do love Sara so much and if we had to pick a realistic scenario for a girl to end up with I would pick her. I also want her to have a happy ending, I look forward to her purity route very much.

The rest right this minute, could change next minute:
Love: Wakana, Yumi, Makoto, Rin, Molly, Touka, Kaori, Chinami, Maki, Futaba, Chika (non crazy version, blonde if possible), Uta, Himawari
Like just fine/Sometimes Love: Yuki, Karin, New Osako, Io, Noriko, Haruka, Sana, Tsuneyo, Miku, Kirin, good Ami versions
Really grown on me lately: Tsukasa, Yasu, Otoha
Don't dislike: Imani, Rika, Nao-chan
Pretty much hate, most of the time: Tsubasa, Nodoka, bad Ami versions

posts.content_html_raw:
Day 28 character count 16471. Someone should really tell me if I'm going overboard with the length of these but I feel like If I have to ask, the answer is probably yes. The quality won't go up just because the quantity goes down tho, so there's that.
Yumi working at a maid cafe? Now that would be something.

If there was a way to look at the different things from the past mentioned, like the school uniform Maya and Ami used to wear, that would have been great, but right now I'm basically reading this dialogue with a blank image in my mind.

I mean to be fair... Yasu's last school refused to talk about her and everything about and surrounding her is just weird. It wouldn't be too absurd to imagine that the school just turn a blind eye to whatever she's wearing in school for some reason.
And yeah, I feel like I noticed Maya's uniform changing at some point but don't think I pointed it out.

Oof, Maya! That's a bit rude! Poor Ami is always gonna be flat at this rate. Ami was gonna save up for new clothes for when her chest grows and Maya said she could just stop working there now. Savage.

I'm still trying to grasp what brought Maya to want to try to have sex with him out of desperation of having the world she knew crumbling. I think there are just too many different time, space and memory anomaly's going on at once for me to make sense of the severity of that happening. It could be as simple as upwards of a couple years to something like potentially hundreds to thousands of even millions of years. I would perhaps understand her desperation better if we go by the thousand or million year theory. Perhaps the last time it happened had something to do with Noriko after all and it changed everything so drastically that Maya just can't mentally handle it all falling apart again so she grasp at straws doing the one thing she absolutely doesn't want to do because it's the only effective solution.
I'm assuming that simply having his personality replaced along with the student happens all the time for her but... well, I fail to see how the entire world can reset. I feel like there is a thought pattern here, some previous answers I never made sense of that would explain how it could happen. She just described that he has died and been reset in the past, but it seems he almost got close to somehow causing the world to crumble. Hmmm... I think the scary room was about to reset the world, if it weren't an illusion. That or she was being reset, if not both? I don't feel like I'm making any progress here. Moving on.

If Maya hates Noriko so much, why doesn't she just kill Noriko herself instead of asking the mc to do it? Potential consequences? She haven't done it before and worry how it would affect her?

My god Maya is living a miserable existence... She's no god(as far as I know when it comes to superpowers and such) so her life is just as normal and hurtful as it is for everyone else. She also lives through the same things over and over, having to reexplain everything when one thing goes wrong. She fears the things she says may be the cause of things resetting. She must be absolutely miserable in a way and it would perfectly explain why she feels nothing to the mc while everyone else does. Even if there is a power pushing her and everyone else to fall for him to some degree, her willingness to not grow attached is significantly stronger. The mc has to keep living through every reset for Maya to start growing attached again and given this next reset will take him further than he ever was before.
On a side note, I wonder if she has lived through the special worlds as well. The one where everyone's lust is extremely high, the one where everything is just happier and whatever else kind of warped reality there is. We saw in the scary room... or more like heard, that she was watching the happier world from the happy event "Baby Finches" so that makes me think that maybe that's part of her memory. A world that actually happened. I think I'm definitely on to something.

I wonder why it's a horrible idea for Maya to meet him at his home...? I think back to the 666 lust world but I struggle to see how that could be connected. But I also can't rule it out.

Wtf is that reaction from Osako? It makes me laugh. "These two(referring to Wakana and Osako) are too in love with one another to ever fall for me anyway" proceeded by a nervously laughing and blushing Osako.
Or maybe it's because that's suppose to be a secret the school isn't meant to know about.

Well I just had another thought (I know, it's scary when that happens). What if after some of these resets, some characters suddenly decide to either switch sexual preferences or go from lesbian to bi and that's how they will be included in the harem? Would that be a crazy thought to have?

I imagined Osako's and Wakana's relationship and now I imagine Wakana as a dominant bottom(because she's intimidating, unwavering and lazy) and Osako as the submissive top(because she's well trained and that blush earlier gave me the impression she gets embarrassed too easily to dominate anyone she is attracted to). Huh...

This game puts a lot of thought into "name and I/me" and "I/me and name" and it makes me uncomfortable because it's not teaching me cheat, I'm not native and the vast majority of people probably don't care about this because it's combating what they have already learned, how they think it should be and how it sounds and so on.

To say Maya's weakness is food is almost an understatement.

Love that Wakana is so good at bringing out Osako's embarrassed side.

Maybe Osako SHOULD kill him after all. He did just decide to tell Maya about her blindfold kink...

Man, I hate proposal baits. Intentionally getting someone's hopes up and then crushing them. It's just sadistic and 100% worth breaking up over. Reminds me of my hate for wasting perfectly good cakes by pushing the important person's head into it. I would out of spite not invite that person to any parties again and retire from the party prematurely. Let everyone suffer for that stupid prank.

I don't think calling Uta cute has any effect on her.
Is there anything that's not cold or heat that can make Uta blush? I don't think I've seen that before. I just know she apparently doesn't get embarrassed.

I have a similar ish family situation to Uta.
My half brother got himself into trouble with the law too and it was pretty lit...

Suspicious. "I'm not really sure if I agree with uprooting your entire life for the sake of-" for the sake of what? Somehow he cut himself off mid sentence almost like he was about to say something his body did not want him to say. Think that had happened before.
I don't believe for a second she cut herself off saying "And I love yo-" because she wanted to mess with him.
Oh shit, she can blush after all. Holy fuck, he managed to catch her of guard but I'm barely keeping up with this conversation.
Yeah, "This is...new" indeed.

Oof, Ami! "I will destroy everything you love." Directed at Haruka. The only 2(3?) things she loves is the cafe, her husband (and Sensei?).

A good majority of the internet would agree with Haruka that Black Widow is the hottest avenger. Me? Not much to choose from if you are a straight male. I have no idea who The Scarlet Witch is but those seem to be the only 2 so ehh.

Uh oh, here comes trouble. Ami sure loves to get home too early. I don't quite remember how badly it went last time, but I don't imagine Ami seeing Haruka at home again is a good thing.
God damnit, Ami! Asking Haruka about her marriage is so much worse than complaining and being suspicious that she's here!
And calling her a whore. Wtf has gotten into Ami now?
And Ami has the audacity to ask if she's crying... So insensitive. This is how you drop off.
And calling her a fucking slut.
And saying you don't want him catching any STDs. Also how the fuck do you think Haruka will interpret the part about "that might impact how much time he gets to spend with me"?
Wtf? Day 29 character count 9802, 1,828 words.
Six thousand cups of tea. I think Wakana may have a problem...

Yuki at the gym. She just keeps getting more intimidating.
Nodoka has a thing for Yuki... I can't tell if I'm surprised by this or not.
Oh god, these two are so thirsty for Yuki!
Also I just noticed she's using that band aid thing to hide her tattoo. I think that band aid has a Japanese name but I don't remember it
Okay that cracked me up! "Hi Rin. Don't look down." "Of course I'm going to look down if you tell me not- oh (blushes, eyes widen)"
Nodoka is hopeless...

Did the mc really just fucking ask "what is XD"? My god... I feel like people his age used to use that stuff back in the day, how the fuck does he not know this stuff?

Walked into Yasu's room for that repeatable hangout thing and OH MY GOD why are you so close? Stop it!

That could have been bad... Futaba talking to her mom and the mc blurting out that his teaching her how to pleasure a man. She is not amused...

So... Futaba wants her shadow to be more like his... then literally don't change anything, you are big and he has a lot of muscles on account of being a man... This analogy or whatever is stupid because it's contradictive to what she's actually asking for. I don't think wanting a shadow that's more like a male really works when first of all, you are not a male and secondly, men are larger in their upper body.
Welp, at least she finally told him about the eater disorder.
OH SHIT, I didn't connect those dots earlier! She's trying to make herself throw up to lose weight! I don't know if that even works, it feels like it's more destructive than good, at least mentally speaking.

If there is one thing the game is adamant about, it's hammer in this idea that no matter how much you tell someone you don't care or how they look and you try to force them to accept themselves be less self conscious and all that, it doesn't really work. I can't see that from my perspective and I'm probably just as guilty as the mc is here and my words would probably not reach Futaba either. Now I'm not as accepting as the mc about body size and nor do I want to lie but there are some things that have nothing to do with body size that I really don't mind. Things like breast size. I may prefer them on the smaller side but if someone wants them bigger for their own game it's hard to differentiate between their own personal want and your desire for them to listen to you and approve and accept themselves.

Ah, bulimia. Never heard of before but at least that's a word to search up.

Now he said it... I had sorta hoped he would say that was Yumi's mom earlier when all three were around.
This can't be the first time Futaba had chain events. I don't see the obsession with giving Futaba so many events.

Has anyone been keeping count to the number of times "that one thing(the kiss with Yumi)" has been referenced?

Yumi having an extra bad day today it seems.
And it just got 10 times worse for her... Mc, if you are gonna let something like that slip about Yumi's mom, you might as well tell her not to bring it up in front of Yumi!
Futaba has to suffer the consequences for your carelessness, fuck sake dude...
And there is another giant L from the mc. Doesn't fucking tell Yumi right away that it was his slip up to say that was Yumi's mother. Stupid fucking mc.
Of course he goes and tells Yumi about it AFTER Yumi threatens to kill Futaba and say all that other mean shit. I fucking swear this mc is unbearable sometimes.
Wonder if Yumi calling herself an accident was her knowing the truth or just insulting herself without knowing it.
If you fucking cared about Futaba at all you would have told her AFTER accidentally letting that slip about it being her mother! You have no excuse, you are a disappointment of an mc!

Sometimes I wonder how this wonderful this game would be if the mc was at least somewhat competent in dealing with people.

Okay that's creepy... That Ayane dojo event that's totally generic and nothing special going on but more Ayane being Ayane. The music stopped at the end and the mc said he can't help but shake the feeling there is something looming in the background. Ummmmmm...?

immediately proceeding by another event hinting at doors that can't be opened ever again.

So first something looming in the background and now Ayane is keeping her distance...

Is what legal? Hire an ex yakuza who did drugs? Who knows. Probably not what the Sakakibaras' were talking about anyway.


Is it really as simple as Ayane missing her mom? I don't buy that. But it's not like you don't get those moments of sudden vulnerability for certain thoughts occasionally. Like depression in general. Most of the time you can be fine and then you suddenly have a really sad day.
"Listen to the loli, Sensei!" HAHA!
Sana really wants a baby. Yep, lets go with that, that is totally what she said.

There are a lot of hints that the actual story takes place only in Akira's head.
His talk with Chinami for example, what lies beyond the walls. A monster, behind the monster another monster. Smells like he's afraid to face reality.
Not to forget "This town/city has two halves", like a brain/mind.
The walls being the border of his mind/brain/skull, going beyond meaning trying to wake up.

For me, the most probable outcome for the story is that it all happens in his head while he is still in coma for whatever reason (Sekai's death or whatever).
Technically it will also give Sel an excuse for dropping lore points and that most of the mystery does not need to make sense.
It's like only story start, end and some sprinkles within that have some meaning, while most of the story is neglectable.

I read those Nodoka lines as more of a staring down the barrel of the camera 4th wall breaking moment. She wonders if she is a voice inside someone's head. And she is, in that very moment and in general, a voice inside you, the readers, head. She wonders if there is someone that takes shelter in the idea of her existence. "The idea of my existence" well that is essentially what a character is really. The idea of someone that you construct from the words on the page and the "voices in your head". It is a love story, but it extends through the 4th wall. She wonders if there is someone reading it that loves her character. And the line about "is it possible to fall in love with them -- enjoy the company you create rather than the company you find" is kind of a thesis of a meta commentary of the genre as a whole, fiction in general or even in some ways everyone playing the game.

I don't know the literary terms to say what I'm thinking properly but maybe that makes some sense. Whether her character is or is not explicitly speaking to the reader ultimately doesn't really mater. It still fits with what her character is doing and thinking. That is, trying to figure out the nature of the world they are in, ect. Or to word it differently, it would not be out of character for such thoughts to cross her mind.

posts.content_html_raw:
With regards to those old discord comments, I found them a bit devious because 'hallucinations' do not fall under 'simulation' or 'it's all a dream.' This is to say I can clearly imagine a reality where Sensei is hallucinating 99% of what's happening, OR everything that's happened is framed as a book / game he's reading/playing, yet this would evade classification as "simulation" or "all a dream." Of course, in the first place, I'm not really dead-set on figuring out THE TRUTH and cracking THE PUZZLE, but when it comes to strong allusions that things are going on in Sensei's head, I am disinclined from throwing them out wholesale. For example, at this point I would be pleasantly surprised if Ami/Ayane/Maya are 'real' living people and not hallucinations, but even if they are hallucinations, I wouldn't interpret that as 'dream theory' it'd be a more elaborate 'how real are how hallucinations / how real is fiction if it affects us irl / it may be fake to us but it's real to them' etc type stuff.

By the way, at risk of implied spoilers, I would once again invite fans of LiL to read Subahibi. It is the same kind of "spew vomit from the bottom of your mind and call it a visual novel" kind of thing that LiL is. Which is not to say LiL fans would like it (in fact, I myself found it quite a chore to get through), but it is highly enriching when analyzing LiL since it's one of the main inspirations for it. Worst come to worst you can come out with more ammo for calling Sel a hack or something.

Mon panache!

People like Sel anticipate being hated. That's why by default they wear masks - just look at his initial patreon posts, where he is gushing with appreciation and gratitude for every single player, or the polite affectations he puts on when wanting something. These are the attitudes of someone who knows from life experience they have something to hide - themselves. The darkness for such individuals is filled with screaming and buzzing static noise. A lifetime of punishment just for existing. Behind every external individual is a demon ready to swipe. And so a forum of people shitting on you is just a matter of course - the demons had always been lurking in the darkness. That is why there is the inclination to engage primarily with demons and brush off or entirely ignore the angels. An angel is just a demon in disguise waiting to reveal their true colors. Nobody can be trusted. But demons can be slayed. And so I imagine f95 is a comfortable place for him, a home away from home, where he can relish in the wrath he always knew existed.

What would be much more interesting is a forum of people praising Selebus no matter what. There are some accusations of the discord being a cult worshipping Selebus, but they live in fear there and he knows it. He can't really trust or believe them, I think. Just look at how he mocked them on F95 as two-faced cheaters hiding their true inclinations from him. So the discord, too, is a place of demons; dedicated fans waiting to turn on him and shit on him the moment the loli content gets too extreme or what have you.

How would Selebus respond in heaven, though? How would he respond to the unconditional, overflowing affection of thousands upon thousands of people? THAT would be more interesting. And perhaps it's what we're seeing in Lessons in Love.

Gameboy things? Oof, he probably just upset a lot of people with that line.

Tsuneyo is a good dog.

And the roof no less... Considering Maya isn't here either, I dunno what that means. Maya IS in the manga club right? Should be.

Just casually pointing out Ayane's vaginal depth out of nowhere...

Would it be crazy if the world "ended" right here, Ayane disappeared and he therefore arrived before Maya did and she spouts some nonsense about how it's a miracle his here first and he tells her he came to see Ayane or something and she says his disgusting?

Demons can jump 10 feet into the air? We should ask Kirin just to fact check that for us.

Ayane catching onto his missing memories. And she knows about Ami's non niece related love for him. Not too surprising.

She pushes him away for a reason and she did mention and we did see that he apparently hallucinates her as an animal when things get rough and sex might be on the line. So in a world where he could lift the curse on his memories and she didn't have to fear his hallucinations and violent reactions to memories, is it possible that they have a stronger bond than anyone else and that Ayane is right about him picking her? Ayane did mention that he looks at Maya differently but is she aware that might be become of the mutual knowhow of the reset phenomena and Maya is sort of an intentionally limited guide? Who knows.

That's a BIIIIIG moon. Are they not gonna talk about that? The sky sure is interesting, but I would be concerned about a moon that's like, right there, probably over 10 times the size.

Something big happened but she won't tell you just yet and that's where the "nevermind" part of the event name comes in. That's not ominous at all...

There's a lot of pain in that crying of Ayane's, but the source is not easy to find. Is it just Ayane being Ayane or is there something more to it?

Yep, that doesn't look right. Wth happened to the house and why is the music so happy?
So he JUST came home after being with Ayane and now the disappearance decided to happen... also wtf does "are you house" mean and why is he talking straight into my soul when saying that? Get away you creep!

And now his T-posing in the bed... this man is a lunatic.
Tsuneyo's shirt smilie has breached containment again. God damnit.

Another number I'm not gonna write down because I am a filthy puzzle txt thing user. I am smart, but not smart enough for this.

What does that even mean? I'm trapped in my real bedroom? Gotta be a metaphor and not in a more literal sense.

Guess this game doesn't use a voice slider or whatever, because this mini section is voice which is... interesting. Just a problem that it's put on the volume slider and is quiet as fuck while the banging sounds would be deafening if I increase the volume.

God fucking damnit. Need to manually translate all of that.
You know what? Nevermind. It all just seems to be the names of the characters and if it's not then shit. There is one that just translates to t so...

A redhaired teacher... bet she also wants our money. I wonder if the numbers on the clocks show up later or if the happy event is the only way to see that?

The old Maya judging by the shirt. Ami in a childish pink dress and I'm guessing that would be Noriko? Also the mc's head is rotated 180 degrees and his facing the other direction. What a lovely sight...

Maya doesn't even get the chance to ask questions...

Wtf am I looking at? A shadow reaching through the ground to grab at creepy animal masks?

I don't think they are nearly old enough in this pic to be learning about sex toys.
Special after class activities... she's gonna take our money, I fucking knew it!

The teacher DOES hear Maya after all and somehow Ami turned into a blobfish... or her head did. How lovely. She can finally be herself.
What a mean teacher. Wanting to poison Maya like that.

WAIT A GOD DAMN MINUTE! I remember this woman now. I shouldn't know who she is yet but I know she looks suspiciously similar to Ami and has the same last name. So a good chance that's her Ami's mother or something. It's not like hiding the fact I downloaded the koikatsu portraits long ago changes anything but it is one of the sources for my forbidden knowledge so.

Ami, don't look!
Welp, that was fucking weird. As usual.

Ok yeah, so it's not just character names.
One of them translates to Saki and conveniently that is the name most similar to this mystery woman fromt he happy event and ALSO prompts the game to say he goes back in time. Now I'm no expert but it all seems to lead back to this being Ami's mom. Question is if somehow she is still alive or will be or if this is some memory exclusive thing.

HAHA wtf! Why did I find that so funny? He screamed into the phone and it screamed back so he got scared, he called himself.

Oh, the animal heads meant something. I would probably be so lost without the txt thingy.

The last time the sky was static, he ran into Yumi way back. Or at least I think that was the last time...

What do you do when your legs start talking and disobey your commands?

But now is the opportunity to surprise Maya... Who knows, maybe she will be so surprised she wants to do the sex... Sorry, I think these events are having an effect on me.

Yeah I don't. I don't think the US would agree with having this game as the new standard of religious education.

I still don't know what that thing behind Jesus is suppose to be.

Wonder if the mc learning how to dance will somehow have some catastrophic side effects.

"Net with knife nose and melon mouth". How do you even come up with this shit?

Game theory reference... That holds more value now that he has "retired" as far as I'm aware.

Does it change anything that Maya may have memory issues too? Probably not.

I had a feeling she was gonna bring up the test of courage the moment she said she was forced to remember something.

Remind me if I'm wrong but I'm pretty sure the mc HAS seen Ami disappear.

!!! Someone else showed up at the rooftop!?
Oh, well would you look at that! It was Ayane.
It was way to coincidental... Throwing that Ayane event at us right before the reset and at the rooftop no less. She said she didn't know why she went to the rooftop and she is hiding something she decided not to tell him. I'm not sure what to make of this yet but it must freak Maya the hell out. I imagine all those resets, there has never been anyone but Sensei and Maya.
If Ayane remembers this after the reset, I imagine this will just keep happening until everyone is aware of the reset phenomena and everyone start having a minor existential crisis.
Well, next reset probably. If she's made to believe it was a dream.

Must be a scary experience for Ayane. She's seeing a sky she's never seen before, everyone but them are missing and she somehow found herself on the roof not knowing what brought her there.

I'm gonna go out on a whim and assume what Maya meant is that because he keeps having sex with Ayane, somehow that may have formed a bond that somehow allowed her to also show up at the rooftop.

Okay that was... scary turned confusing very fast.
Oh... Well that's weird. Is that a thing some people might experience? Being delusional, forgetting who people are by name and such right after waking up?

Oh yeah, that is weird. Why is Sana here?

This kinda reminds me of the Makoto roof incident. The world rewrote that just like it rewrote this. Ayane doesn't remember ever being at the school rooftop and there was no sleepover for whatever reason. She remembers having a dream but not what that dream was. A very convenient excuse of the world to make her also not remember him asking if she met him and Maya at the rooftop while also making the part about this whole thing being a dream become reality. Can Ayane really not be trusted to know about the resetting going on?

I wonder if anything would happen if he said something like this? "It wasn't a dream. The meeting with me and Maya on the rooftop about resetting the world actually happened. Maya told you to think it was a dream but I didn't expect you to forget it happened in the first place" Would that freak her out, cause some kind of calamity?

What a wakeup call indeed. Ami is so incredibly desperate.

Small changes like Yuki now working at the bar may not mean much but at least it makes the game world feel a little more alive.
Like daughter like mother I guess. Neither of them seem to know how to speak to customers. As long as she doesn't threaten to kill someone she's already more successful than Yumi.

Of course Sana remembers the sleepover and Ayane doesn't... Nothing can ever make sense.

Kirin feigning ignorance by seemingly pretending it's okay to be show up at Ayane's room. I don't remember if Kirin has ever done anything nice for anyone that wasn't sexual.
Like seriously, it's like she's living in her own bubble thinking someone who used to be her friend still is after mentally scaring them repeatedly. Or she's fully aware of her actions and is just being evil for the sake of self pleasure or some future objective. Either way I don't trust her.

How to piss off Miku 101. Mention her flat chest. Congratulations.

Uta's swimsuit burn my eyes and not for a good reason... not that there was a good reason given how I worded that.
"Now, everyone turn around and bend over so I can see the rest of the swimsuits for a more accurate judgement of them." I dunno what to say about this one.
For some reason I can't pinpoint why Futaba is not more nervous being seen in that swimsuit. I feel like I should know the reason.

What...? Oh, is it that the mc stopped paying attention to Uta in favor of Maki that she's now zoning out in concern? She's not getting the attention she wants.

I really wish the distance between the dorm war and beach event wasn't so long. That's a lot of text to skip by and I also have to go through the reset too.

Can't believe Maki is playing alone with this daddy thing but I don't think I should be surprised by this.

UH OH! Makoto slipped up! Instantly snapped the moment the mc asked if there are condoms in the janitors closet by saying "AS IF YOU'D WILLINGLY USE ONE OF THOSE!". Yeah, surely there is no way to talk your way out of that!? HAHAHA! She snapped too quickly implying she didn't have to think and guess because she knows he wouldn't. Got way too emotional about it implying it's a topic she is passionate about which could also imply she's mad at him for not using them. Also she said that sarcastically implying that she once again knows he wouldn't use them which she should only know if she has experience with it. That is a checkmate for all I'm concerned.

"Yumi was here"
"Surprising. Stop writing on the board. - MM"
"Tired? Weak? Come to dorm 9. I will show you the."
"You too, Yasu. - MM"
In true Makoto fashion, lectures everyone using the black board...

I feel like Touka's family could probably help Chinami attend the beach and stuff. Even if the recommended way to avoid infections are always gonna be to just stay home, I'm sure Touka's family either has A: an expensive treatment for Chinami or B: a functional hazmat suit or something similar that's not too restrictive. Money should definitely be able to help Chinami in some form.

Yumi being offended when she's called "the bully" when that's quite literally what she is to Futaba.
RIP Touka.

Oof... Rin planning another confession with Otoha this time. She hasn't known Otoha very long but at least Otoha knows her feeling a hundred times better than Chika seemed to so I feel like it would have been better if she waited longer.

I almost missed that but Molly is giving Rin the sad eyes and Rin doesn't notice.
Oh... ummm, what is Molly about to say...?
Just concerned about her friend. Thought that was gonna be a comical setup for Molly confessing or something. As comical as something that painful can be that is...

Chika: "Come get wet with my sister and me." She's not even excusing her phrasing.
Oh god, this is like a golden opportunity! Seeing Yumi in a kiddie pool. I wonder if Chika even told Yumi he was about to show up?
Iirc, she only wears that white shirt because she didn't want the mc staring at her.
Update, she did not know he was coming and is now blushing profusely! Perfect!(if only her white shirt wasn't on tho)
"It's... not what it looks like!" Are you sure about that?
She's so embarrassed being seen that way that she will leave Chinami to fend for herself. Tisk tisk, what a bad older sister Yumi is.
Oh yeah... I am so used to a life where you just have to hope someone doesn't get sick because of you but they won't actually die. So knowing that Yumi prioritized her dignity over Chinami's life in a roundabout way is kinda shitty. Can't be easy for Chinami knowing that she may have to be alone for days at a time if one of them gets sick. But I mean, just MAYBE the mc volunteers to spend some time with Chinami in case that happens since he was the cause of them running out to begin with. Chika should have told Yumi he was coming, Yumi should have not ran out, Chika should have not followed Yumi knowing they might both get sick.
Yumi's body is more womanly than Chika's? I haven't really compared so I can't say if that's true.

And I just now realized that Chika's height is 5.5/167cm and Yumi's is 5.6/166cm... I'm confused.

Yumi really got that flustered huh. Where would she possibly go dressed like that? Did she even put on shoes?

You are calling one of your student's little sisters because she's cute and a little menace and if you get on good terms with her, maybe you will get on good terms with the other two?

"I am a grown man sitting at a table with a little girl in a dog mask who is holding a box of strawberry milk for sheer aesthetic purposes."
Otoha has spotted this very peculiar situation.
I really can't grasp what's so wrong about this situation. Sure, if you put words to this it might be weird but most people would just assume it's a father and their strange child and move on with their day. Is it a taboo of some sort in Japan or America? I dunno, but there are certainly a lot more concerning things you can see out in public. 50 felonies? I'm going to pretend that is 50 felonies too many to be accused of and move on.

Rin struggling to figure out where she heard the name Chinami before and his not even helping her right away. Does he just like to see people struggle?
Rin gets lovestruck hearing Otoha barking like a dog... Rin is so down bad and I love it.

It must be kinda awkward and sad for Otoha to be there during this exchange.

Just like that? This just felt like a normal meeting between mc and Maki at the porn shop and it suddenly turned into a fingering scene.

Karin fears that one sound macaroni and cheese make when you steer it and I can somehow see why someone would be afraid or at least uncomfortable by it.

If Karin had one of the other girls' personality, which one would be the most cursed? It's easy to say Kirin, Nodoka or Maki but I wonder if Wakana's personality would be the most cursed one on Karin. I don't know what brought me to think about this, I just did.

Legends say Maya is still rolling around in a wheelchair thanks to Karin's violent assault with a baseball bat.

I'm starting to feel like Kirin is just a character made so that the player have someone to hate. She's a menace to Karin too and Karin is describing her as a hypocrite whose allowed to have fun and have friends and Karin isn't. She doesn't use the word hypocrite tho but it's definitely implied.

that poor table...

I wouldn't read that much into it though because it's one of those things that Selebus used a lot during the first chapters and then dropped into the later ones. The use of different "God, GOD, GoD, god" seems to only point out that there are many of them (since at that point in the game, that is something that is being presented through reset narration and happy events). And a secondary simpler reason is that Akira himself doesn't believe in god, thus using lowercase, even though he clearly exists and so his consciousness has to correct itself from that hidden knowledge God god.

Yasu, for instance, only recognizes one god, which is HOPE (quite a young one too) - but Yasu has a skewed vision of things as they are, as HOPE himself recognizes Wires - and later how much skewed that vision is presents itself to her. Pareidolia, for obvious reasons, recognizes lots of them from the start. Furthermore, we're shown many times during chapter 4 that a lot of gods exists anyway - many more than different ways to write the word god would account for.

This is a post that speculates on a sentence I always have trouble to find, and that remains a mystery to me. It deals with the nature of Nao-chan, and which forces she represents in the divine struggle. But the post itself offers no real answer, so bear that in mind. If you'd like to skip the speculation, here's the sentence:

"[...]the songs unmatching eyes doth sing to the choirs of we sodomites. [...] It will take more than a color wheel to eradicate this parasite."
This text comes to Akira in a dream as Nao-chan makes her way into their house.




Well, one can assume "Mommy" refers to either Sekai, Saki or Tsubasa (?). Most likely Sekai due to the nature of the poem, and that it is a poem.

So we have Sekai saying that unmatching eyes sing to the choirs of sodomites. That is either Kaori (which hosts many gods), or Nao-chan, which was sent to Kaori/Akira to help them. Nao-chan can't speak however much less sing, neither of them are really pretentious either.

The most interesting sentence is "it will take more than a color wheel to eradicate this parasite". That puts the heterochromia girls against the parasite (either Sekai, Pareidolia, or any of the gods hosted by Kaori).

Then it seems to address Akira, telling how when he's safe, he strays from his "true nature". Lastly, the thing about being carved into their chest fits both Akira and Kaori, since Sekai is still with him and with her as well (physically so in the case of Kaori).
After this, Akira goes around with Nao-chan through his home, the mall, and the old district - wherever he goes by, Nao-chan captures the love of anyone she comes in contact with. But Akira is aware that something is following him all the way (always reminding him of his vile impulses).
Another point of note is that Nao-chan literally dresses all in blue, which is a callback to what the narrator says during the fight between Ayane/Maya and Ami - that you can trust one of them, that they left clues everywhere and that they're dressed in blue. Which we tend to interpret as Ayane as she's in the scene, hears the narrator, it is her chapter, and Himawari is her daughter. But who knows (because this is right after he leaves Nao-chan and Kaori in "where the fieldmice run", so it could still fit).
Mind you, the reason Akira runs to Kaori that night is because something is following him, and Sekai/Pareidolia seemingly help him by having Kaori kiss him with Sekai's tongue, which serves to numb him for a time.

My point being that the thing following him is likely the same in both cases. If that something is the "Old one" that is summoned during Noriko's inviteover, or simply a representation of Akira's darker impulses is unknown.

It'd be interesting if what is following him is simply himself. Pareidolia would point that out many times over the course of Chapter 4. It would also justify Pareidolia's role as someone that makes himself the scapegoat to Akira's acts.

One of the things Akira says during the bus ride with Nao-chan also seems to point into that direction in a narration I had forgotten:

He needs to protect, yet he doesn't know why. This struggle between his dark nature and the essence of fatherhood would be reintroduced as the thing that got him out of the bed after the Maya tragedy, as he focuses on being a dad to Ami. This idea of Akira being "redeemed" through being a parent is something that is also referenced by the narrator when they say "I'm everything you've never wanted, but all you'll ever need" (I forgot when, but likely the second half of chapter 3) - which I tend to interpret as Himawari talking about him having a daughter.
Anyway, I'll keep observing Nao-chan through the replay, and hopefully be able to understand a little bit more about TEMPLATE 9's role in all of this.

Well, one can assume "Mommy" refers to either Sekai, Saki or Tsubasa (?). Most likely Sekai due to the nature of the poem, and that it is a poem.

So we have Sekai saying that unmatching eyes sing to the choirs of sodomites. That is either Kaori (which hosts many gods), or Nao-chan, which was sent to Kaori/Akira to help them. Nao-chan can't speak however much less sing, neither of them are really pretentious either.

The most interesting sentence is "it will take more than a color wheel to eradicate this parasite". That puts the heterochromia girls against the parasite (either Sekai, Pareidolia, or any of the gods hosted by Kaori).

It's not just the images, as i understand it the game's engine will compile all .rpy files into .rpyc files every time you load the game, this is one of the ways that Renpy makes it easy to add to or mod the game, just throw an .rpy in and reload, but it does mean, with how many .rpy files LiL has and how long many of them are that it's basically recompiling a lot of the game on every boot for no reason. I do know you can take previously compiled .rpy files out to speed things up, but i found it too finicky for too small a gain, easier to just double click the .exe and do something else for a minute or two, enjoy the music when it finally loads.

Again, I don't want to spoil, so I'll say this:

LiL is a game about a seriously fucked up person trying to deal with incomprehensible trauma, and his successes and failures. I can't tell you how to judge him or any other character in the game, but that's the point. It asks questions. It asks questions that are hard and uncomfortable and fucked up. But that's the point, in many ways.

Is sensei a good person: objectively, no, he is not. Is he trying to get better and find better morals? Probably? I mean, that's part of the question the game asks. It isn't a light game in any way, and it isn't for anyone that isn't ready to tackle questions that are generally too divisive for most media.

But that is part of the beauty of LiL. Its asking questions that are usually hidden and censored and watered down. And its messy and uncomfortable and some scenes will make you grimace at having to make a choice! And if that isn't your jam, more power to you! But if you want to confront situations that will legitimately make even the most calloused person take pause, then proceed forward. But never feel bad for saying "This is my limit, I'm done with this." either.

EDIT:

One of the strengths of this game is how it leverages the fact that the reader is separate from the MC. To answer this question rigorously we'd have to agree on definitions for identity and agency, and how those two relate with fiction and the telling of narrative. He's definitely not a good person, but whether or not that has and will always be is a point of conention as we await future chapters. If you chose to continue to play this game, be mindful of the speaker of a given textbox. The narration often alludes to having a specific speaker, but the game won't flat out tell who is talking, or to whom the narration is directed towards.
You have choices that lock you out of scenes, but this game is ultimately a linear experience; the missed paths don't change the destination.

Not quite. There are no branching paths in the way vns use that term. The player can influence certain choices, which prevent some events from being viewed, but these do not cause a split / branch in paths. The fandom likes to say there are only two paths, "Green path" which means seeing all events, and "Red Path" which means missing a couple here and there.

Even so, I would struggle to describe this game's storyline as "clear". The complexity of the story is due to how it's written and the content within, not any player choices. You can't make MC any more of a bad person than he already is, but you can't make him a good boy either.

You should use the guide mod, and maybe save a decent amount. I basically save whenever I think a important choice is happening that the hint mod hasn't told me results in missing events. If you don't make backups like this, you can lose time every now and then. If you do lose progress like this and the save isn't that old, you can just turn on text skip and get back decently quickly.

There is no ending yet, but certain choices will make you miss events and you can't get them back, you'd have to load an old save. We call seeing all the events the green path, we've been told that there will be always a way to see every event, and missing any events is called red path.

If you stay on the green path, you will make bad and worse choices. But there are hints during the game that people have to be broken before they can be made better than ever. Some red choices will make you feel good in the short term, but you can notice some weird things in the dialogue afterward. We don't know for sure if people will get punished for missing events, but the developer has made similar choices before and punished you for them every time so there's a pattern to learn from.The update that came out two weeks ago had a lot of events that only show up if you were still on the green path. The game was definitely partially inspired by DDLC. But in hindsight, DDLC feels like a concept demo in comparison. Both in terms of story length and character depth.
DDLC is rather gimmicky, with a clear focus on subverting expectations, the contrast between slice of life atmosphere and straight up gore, and re-defining psychological horror within a VN gameplay loop.

LiL borrowed some of its themes from the first two points, while the gameplay is about as creative as unseasoned cooked boiled potatoes.
At the end of the day though, they are not really comparable titles. LiL is a story-rich game that focuses on character development, lore and mystery. The gimmicky DDLC factor acts mostly just as a hook in the beginning of the game. The meat and potatoes lie in the dialogues and character interactions and only gets to fully bloom in the long run.
Also idk why I'm thinking of potatoes all the time, I guess I played through too many Molly events lately.

posts.content_html_raw:
Objectively speaking, Otoha still is an awful dating material and an occasionally comical douche nozzle. Despite of that, however, she has uniquely become this rare and mostly consistent positive influence on Sensei ever since Maya Prime died, a feat seldom achieved by the rest of her classmates who actually love the man.

But perhaps it is because of exactly that, Otoha ironically surpasses almost the entire harem when it comes to reaching to him as a friend instead of as an auxiliary concubine of his. What Otaha does this Christmas to me feels really close to what Rika did back when Sensei went back to school for the first time in Ch4, forcing him to acknowledge that there ARE people who will want to be his friends and will care about him without wanting his penis™.

As someone who grew up almost never receiving any gift and thus also had a hard time grasping the idea of platonic exchange like this one as a kid, this simple “I can really have that?” speaks to me so much. It almost sounds like Sensei is in complete disbelief that there will be someone out there who doesn’t want to have sex with him yet can just genuinely want to care for his wellbeing, even if there is no redeeming quality the said person can really see in him according to his own mindset. It forcefully challenges that mindset of him considering himself being utterly unlikable if his penis isn’t involved, and I think it can really help Sensei move away from always thinking with his dick if he so chooses to grow up one day.

Even if the gift eventually turns out to be very comical, to me it’s quite apparent that the emotional weights between the two “matching” pocketknives are nowhere near matching, to a point that it feels like he actually feels unworthy when he realizes he is incapable of returning a gift to her on the spot. Because how effective the pocketknife he didn’t ask for positively shakes him, I personally would put this just slightly below Yumi’s secret Santa note in terms of emotional values.

I'm 100% convinced that all purity routes are locked behind green path. Game is pretty explicit in that we have to fully degrade ourselves until we are allowed to heal
Click to expand...
I'm not super sympathetic to this perspective due to all the miscellaneous ways in which one can lock themselves out of the green path. Off the top of my head, picking 'kill Kirin' is arguably a pretty malicious/degrading action, yet it blocks off one of her events. So you need to be conscientious to stay on green path, not the opposite. I feel like the only reason Green path even exists as we know it is because of Selebus's professed completionism autism for always 100%ing a visual novel (many such cases among weebs). I expect it would also punish people treating the game more seriously / with more immersion (for example: those who accept being a bad homie instead of reloading to alter their action to avoid consequences), while rewarding primarily URM-users and completionism autists, so it wouldn't cleanly accomplish the artistic goal of forcing players to degrade themselves. That said, I definitely wouldn't be surprised if green path did end up being necessary, it just doesn't seem super likely to me right now.

Fire Lord Zuko said:
Whatever the ending of LiL will be, it won’t be the dream/coma/it’s all in Akira’s head ending.

It’s been deconfirmed by Selebus on at least two separate occasions that I could find:
Click to expand...
Even if for some reason you don't trust Sel's statements on discord, I don't think there's any chance he'd use an "it was all a dream/hallucination/simulation" ending after putting lines like these in the game:

...
Moonflare said:
"[...]the songs unmatching eyes doth sing to the choirs of we sodomites. [...] It will take more than a color wheel to eradicate this parasite."
Click to expand...
My take: During the camping trip, Kaori and Nao ("unmatching eyes") go looking for a machine that can be used to change people's color (a "color wheel"). Kaori's color is green on the outside but red on the inside because of the Sekai inside of her, so it's logical to assume that changing her color could involve eradicating her Sekai "parasite". Similarly, Sensei's color is supposed to be clear, but it's become much darker in chapter 4 because of his own parasite (Pareidolia aka "the dark"), and Kaori says his color is the first one she'll fix. And then there is also the parasite inside of Ami - the "worm" that she wants to cut out in "Della".

Possibly connected, though I don't know how: in "Frankincense & Myrrh" Yasu wants to sing her god's song to a choir of sodomites.
Moonflare said:
Mind you, the reason Akira runs to Kaori that night is because something is following him, and Sekai/Pareidolia seemingly help him by having Kaori kiss him with Sekai's tongue, which serves to numb him for a time.
Click to expand...
At least in a figurative sense, the thing that follows Sensei is Sekai and his traumatic memories of her. In "Frankincense & Myrrh" Yasu says that "ghosts of the past" can follow you and offers to "reveal the voice" of the one following Sensei. By bringing the thing following him to Kaori, he allows it to wake up SeKaori; as they step outside, Kaori tells him to show her the thing following him and he talks about how he's trying to run away from his memories of Sekai, which causes her eyes to start changing.

The kiss with SeKaori is not a good thing for Sensei, but rather another case of him running away from anything difficult.
The event starts with him in a positive mood because of the feelings he has for the girls he's building relationships with.



But burying his feelings was how he dealt with his trauma (hence why he couldn't write anymore after the accident), so with the return of his feelings comes the return of his memories and his pain. Sensei is a coward, so he'll do anything to avoid that; in this case, seeking physical comfort from "Kaori".



Then the kiss starts and he begins to feel numb, which makes him think this is how he's supposed to be: confused, afraid, and using sex as an escape. It's easier for him if he avoids caring for anyone else.



He claims this is a good thing, things weren't actually looking up, and now he's back on the "right course". But this supposed "right course" is the path to becoming the Collector, just like Pareidolia and Sekai want. They want him to become numb and discard his feelings for the girls so that he'll fuck anything and everything without moral compunctions.



After the numbness wears off, he begins the next event ("Worry Not, The Mason Jar") by doing another 180. Things are looking up, feelings are a good thing. He needs to accept having feelings and confront his trauma, not hide away in numbness and meaningless sex.



This is a major theme of the game: you have to face your fears and allow yourself to break in order to ultimately grow as a person. Accepting the "comfort" offered by SeKaori is the antithesis to that.
Moonflare said:
I got through it, I'm victorious again. With URM it's much easier, but still a pain the ass.
Click to expand...
There's a simple way to get through "Amy" which doesn't require URM or keeping track of anything. After you make a choice, rollback isn't disabled until the next choice is shown, so as soon as you see "we've already been over here", you can rollback and choose a different direction. There'll still be a few times where all of the choices lead to repeat rooms, but it's really not that bad. I tried replaying the event while skipping dialogue and it took me two minutes (with no prior memory of the correct path).

"Heeeeey, Miku. How was your penis?" NICE JOB, MAKOTO! HAHAHAHAHA!

Will I ever like Yasu more than this knowing she's the one spouting all the religious and nonsensical nonsense?

I wonder who will have suffered the most as a result of this beach trip? Molly or Rin?

WHAT! cousin!?

Also expected something grand but didn't see how Kaori and something grand would associate but no, perfectly executed. Rambling.
Didn't the accident in question sound like an explosion? This theory would entirely explain everything to my memory. Her memory issues, the spider obsession, the explosion sound, the reason why Yumi never got to hear about it, the hospitalization with machines involved... also her eccentric behavior as the explosion could have damaged her brain. Holy shit, that might be it.

Ahh, well there you have it. She behaved normal back when she and Yumi used to hang out but her sense of clothing is likely still the same. So her general personality and tastes are the same but other parts of her brain responsible for speech pattern and other stuff likely got damaged. It's possible that her brain didn't get damaged and it's all just the result of extreme trauma rebuilding parts of the brain responsible for hiding it all to help her cope. I think it's just that I prefer the... logical explanation over the "brain does weird things after trauma" explanation? What do you even call those two comparisons?

Well I can sort of understand why Yumi wouldn't want to walk into Kaori's life again knowing how she sees other weird people but I think unlike her mom and unlike all the other strangers, I would want to encourage her to get along with Kaori, or at least try. Also Yumi could learn to cope with weird people by associating with someone who used to be her friend but is now a little on the eccentric side. Turn clouds into candy, smile on the sun, raining candy. I will just pretend Yumi was referring to the turn clouds into candy part.
aaaand she's gone. How can you be mid sentence, have a memory lapse, she disappears and then continue the sentence right after? I feel like memory lapses shouldn't work like that.

Yep, here we go. Time for heartbroken Rin episode 2.
There is a noticeable height difference between these two. Why is it so hard for me to grasp that Otoha is tall?
Rin is the queen of going on weird tangents when she's talking to her crush. Haha.
Otoha feels helpless. She can't stop this confession.
Interesting that Rin knows what slow and steady wins the race when she's already confessing.
I almost feel bad for Otoha at this point.
Damnit Rin... You're fucking adorable but you should treat that heart of yours better.

You know what the worst part about all this is? I've been going this whole time on the tangent that Rin is gonna get rejected but the entire fucking time there was something in the back of my mind screaming at me "No, Otoha is gonna accept!" but I've been suppressing that so hard because it just seems ridiculous.
I just feel fucking lost dude. So what's the implication behind this? I feel like Otoha is only saying yes out of pity. She wants to learn what it means to love and between Rin and Sensei, Rin wins on an overwhelming margin on multiple aspects there.

Re: Himawari hallucination/dream quotes; some brief exposition on minor thoughts

I know that the game explicitly mocks the idea of being a simulation, being hallucinations, dreams, etc, all this not-real stuff... and normally, this would be enough to dispel the ideas entirely. It's not like I'm drawn to hallucinatory business because I want it to be true; in fact, it's the opposite. Rather, I'm drawn to it because I REALLY... REALLY... REALLY believe that Selebus is the type to be drawn to the idealistic interpretation of hallucinations being real. Or like: let's say he had a plant in his room named Fred. And every day he talked to this Fred. He ends up with Fred having an elaborate backstory and personality. In this moment, I would not imagine Selebus to say: "and Fred was just a hallucination lmao, he wasn't real." I imagine that Fred would have some special significance to him by that point.

Or in other words, I would say that while Selebus is intrigued by the fakeness attribute of his characters, he is also insistent on their realness; they are both creations of his head yet real beings - just like a hallucination may be. To me, imagining characters as hallucinations from Sensei or like projections of a psyche, etc, is beyond the level of writing them off as mere simulations or the game as a 'dream' to wake up from. So, ultimately, despite the red flags, I continue to be compelled by these things. In the end, an elder god or mystical leyline or fantastical well or psychedelics drugs making weird shit happen is all basically equivalent. At the end of the day, is there REALLY a huge distinction between Key magic creating a world through the power of friendship vs an elder god giving life to fantasies through dark magicks? It doesn't seem that way to me. And so I tend more often than not to forget all the mockery the game has for this stuff.

P.S. some various things of the top of my head which strongly reinforce a core element of non-realness to me:
1) Maya being half-transparent/invisible
2) Himawari shapeshifting (which fooled Nodoka on top of Sensei)
3) The city not existing outside of Sensei's awareness
4) Characters being slave to some kind of script (nobody coming to help Miku when she screamed)
5) The convenience of the world
6) Seasons/systems impacting minds
7) The diegetic text saying 'this is a game'
8) Honestly, it's really fucking weird to imagine that Sensei would have three colorcoded (red blue green) loli waifus waiting on him hand and feet from the start of the game. Like we kind of accept it at the start of the game since it's a central conceit and we don't really know any better but in retrospect I can totally imagine Sensei alone in his cold, empty house just pretending to have a bunch of teenage girls hanging around to kill time. Then like imagine all those shots of him walking to school with them, it's almost like you could cut them out with scissors and see him trudging to school alone, and this is just like------ (ry

At this point there is a degree of strained-ness when it comes to explaining the weirdness without approaching an explanation close to 'it was a simulation.' I think a big thing here is that western authors REALLY love their cleverness. I have read SEVERAL western novel series that end on a godlike character stating "and in fact, everything you've read was a story I was writing!" while very pleased with themselves for their ingenuous conception. So I never over-estimate authors when it comes to feeling THEIR twist TOTALLY isn't simulation ending it's a GENIUS take on fiction and how we interact with it.

That said, I would ABSOLUTELY be pleased as punch if everything was flatly objective to an extremely high degree with maximal unquestioned agency for every character. Like, inarguably, everything we've seen occurred with minimal simulation-approaching-magic or agency denying mishaps or fiction-related twists. That is something I would be very happy about. These are not theories I come up with because I'm always seeking answers and I desperately want to feel clever myself for solving that it was all a hallucination. These are just the base thoughts I have upon considering what I'm reading.

That said, I would ABSOLUTELY be pleased as punch if everything was flatly objective to an extremely high degree with maximal unquestioned agency for every character. spoilers.html:
I know that the game explicitly mocks the idea of being a simulation, being hallucinations, dreams, etc, all this not-real stuff... and normally, this would be enough to dispel the ideas entirely. It's not like I'm drawn to hallucinatory business because I want it to be true; in fact, it's the opposite. Rather, I'm drawn to it because I REALLY... REALLY... REALLY believe that Selebus is the type to be drawn to the idealistic interpretation of hallucinations being real. Or like: let's say he had a plant in his room named Fred. And every day he talked to this Fred. He ends up with Fred having an elaborate backstory and personality. In this moment, I would not imagine Selebus to say: "and Fred was just a hallucination lmao, he wasn't real." I imagine that Fred would have some special significance to him by that point.

Or in other words, I would say that while Selebus is intrigued by the fakeness attribute of his characters, he is also insistent on their realness; they are both creations of his head yet real beings - just like a hallucination may be. To me, imagining characters as hallucinations from Sensei or like projections of a psyche, etc, is beyond the level of writing them off as mere simulations or the game as a 'dream' to wake up from. So, ultimately, despite the red flags, I continue to be compelled by these things. In the end, an elder god or mystical leyline or fantastical well or psychedelics drugs making weird shit happen is all basically equivalent. At the end of the day, is there REALLY a huge distinction between Key magic creating a world through the power of friendship vs an elder god giving life to fantasies through dark magicks? It doesn't seem that way to me. And so I tend more often than not to forget all the mockery the game has for this stuff.

P.S. some various things of the top of my head which strongly reinforce a core element of non-realness to me:
1) Maya being half-transparent/invisible
2) Himawari shapeshifting (which fooled Nodoka on top of Sensei)
3) The city not existing outside of Sensei's awareness
4) Characters being slave to some kind of script (nobody coming to help Miku when she screamed)
5) The convenience of the world
6) Seasons/systems impacting minds
7) The diegetic text saying 'this is a game'
8) Honestly, it's really fucking weird to imagine that Sensei would have three colorcoded (red blue green) loli waifus waiting on him hand and feet from the start of the game. Like we kind of accept it at the start of the game since it's a central conceit and we don't really know any better but in retrospect I can totally imagine Sensei alone in his cold, empty house just pretending to have a bunch of teenage girls hanging around to kill time. Then like imagine all those shots of him walking to school with them, it's almost like you could cut them out with scissors and see him trudging to school alone, and this is just like------ (ry

At this point there is a degree of strained-ness when it comes to explaining the weirdness without approaching an explanation close to 'it was a simulation.' These are just the base thoughts I have upon considering what I'm reading.

I agree in the sense of how Akira perceives it. But it was really hard for me, the reader, to not interpret it as a simple bribe done in order to get her letter/gift/whatever that was to Niki. Thus, it would make Otoha the opposite of what you're saying, she'd simply be manipulating Akira to try to get to Niki, again. Maybe even including him in a threesome idea, since she can't get Niki by herself.

I think it would suit the story for Otoha to become close friends with Akira given that she has burned all bridges and only Nodoka remains as a friend to her. I just don't know that we are there yet in terms of genuine feelings, I hope so though. Just withholding judgement for now.
Click to expand...
It's understandable to a certain extent. Otoha has lost much of everyone's trust, and has to earn it back with future development so that it wouldn't be this easy to assume that the worst of her is still behind the wheel at every turn. Like, I highly doubt Otoha would still bring him any gift IF she already had her closure with Niki so yes, the original post really is more from Sensei's perspective like you said.

Still, I wouldn't go that far and assume all of this is an alleged bribe (with a pocketknife, no less) for a threesome that may or may not happen. The effectiveness of such a random strategy and the lack of eagerness to steer it into the intended direction simply couldn't match a near impossible goal she tries to achieve. Now, it doesn't mean she no longer wants something with Niki to happen, as I think a good chunk of her is still hanging onto a tinge of hope that she will get lucky at some point. And to be fair Otoha has made it quite difficult to defend her for not having the slightest idea of hoping to nudge things into a fantasized path with this gifting gesture. The only two very biased reasons why I am giving her some credits this time are because it's my Otoha effect speaking, and the fact that I genuinely want her to try and be a better person. I would certainly hope she doesn't trash my puny credits too quickly...

If she actually achieves a threesome with a pocketknife, then...maybe I should get some sharp items too...for future development...

I agree in the sense of how Akira perceives it. But it was really hard for me, the reader, to not interpret it as a simple bribe done in order to get her letter/gift/whatever that was to Niki. Thus, it would make Otoha the opposite of what you're saying, she'd simply be manipulating Akira to try to get to Niki, again. Maybe even including him in a threesome idea, since she can't get Niki by herself.
I think it would suit the story for Otoha to become close friends with Akira given that she has burned all bridges and only Nodoka remains as a friend to her. I just don't know that we are there yet in terms of genuine feelings, I hope so though. Just withholding judgement for now.
Click to expand...
It's understandable to a certain extent. Otoha has lost much of everyone's trust, and has to earn it back with future development so that it wouldn't be this easy to assume that the worst of her is still behind the wheel at every turn. Like, I highly doubt Otoha would still bring him any gift IF she already had her closure with Niki so yes, the original post really is more from Sensei's perspective like you said.
Still, I wouldn't go that far and assume all of this is an alleged bribe (with a pocketknife, no less) for a threesome that may or may not happen. The effectiveness of such a random strategy and the lack of eagerness to steer it into the intended direction simply couldn't match a near impossible goal she tries to achieve. Now, it doesn't mean she no longer wants something with Niki to happen, as I think a good chunk of her is still hanging onto a tinge of hope that she will get lucky at some point. And to be fair Otoha has made it quite difficult to defend her for not having the
slightest
idea of hoping to nudge things into a fantasized path with this gifting gesture. The only two very biased reasons why I am giving her some credits this time are because it's my Otoha effect speaking, and the fact that I genuinely want her to try and be a better person. I would certainly hope she doesn't trash my puny credits too quickly...
If she actually achieves a threesome with a pocketknife, then...maybe I should get some sharp items too...for future development...

posts.content_html_raw:
joryuken said:
question how traumatic is the build up towards the green or the red path?
Click to expand...
Red path is just missing stuff, so there's no trauma. I guess there's "trauma" in being a dick to Rin, but that's the outlier. Selebus can't program for shit and (as it is in the current build of LiL) green path should be the one path anyway. This is supposed to be a game that deals with trauma, the player doesn't have enough agency to be their own thing, so yeah, green path has loads of trauma. But so does the rest of the game. Can't really go further without spoilers.
If there was supposed to be choice, then there'd be actual choices. Not "ignore schadenfreude for a million updates in order to get good homie", or "don't see abyss cause otherwise it will trigger Yumi succumbing in Matador". These "choices" can only be made if you have a guide, there's no choice for the regular player.

And I'm not even talking about others that are just "you chose wrong, dumbass", like choosing to kill Kirin in the game, or not choosing Miku over Uta, or not choosing Ayane for a threesome. These choices are literally "if you don't pick this one, it's no content for you! (other than shallow variations of dialogue later)".

The proper choices that you have regarding green/red path in the early game is choosing to sex Sara/Maki/Haruka and Ami. Which, other than Ami, is a strange choice to give because there's no real consistency there - it's not like you can opt out of having sex with other side characters so far. I think Ami is the one choice that makes more sense in the red path, but you lose so much content that it's just baffling.

Granted, in more recent updates there are actual choices such as "pull the plug on Tsukasa or not", or "stomachache or not". It's good that Selebus is learning something. Unfortunately, the writing for the consequences of not having seen stuff is still underwhelming at best.
I'll end by saying that to this date "Stomachache" is the one most traumatic event in terms of general reception, and that's in the green path. But I'll also personally say that "Stomachache" is one of, if not the best event in the game - and kind of the reason as to why this game exists in the first place, aka to depict and discuss trauma in a way that few pieces of work can. It'd be an absolute shame to miss it (or to miss anything for that matter).

Now that I’ve played through the first couple of Yumi events in my newest playthrough, I’d like to post a few thoughts.

After having read previous comments about Yumi’s tsundere nature, I’ve been watching her actions through that lens to see if it holds up, and so far it does. I’ve done the first bullying event at gym, then the subsequent event where she’s called to his office.

The mention previously by lore folks about how she complains about Sensei’s absence at gym class is super interesting, and she does seem annoyed he isn’t there. Even Chika points it out, and Yumi doesn’t deny it, just deflects.

The jealousy angle for Futaba is certainly plausible, given this early on we are told old sensei spent time at the library a lot, but it could still be that she’s targeted because she doesn’t fight back, and that annoys Yumi.

Then there’s the fact Yumi actually shows up when summoned to the office, which, given her outward demeanor, doesn’t make sense; she should just skip it and not care. In her first Streets event, Sensei even says he doesn’t really care if she skips, and she seems a bit flustered, though it’s too early to assign any heavy implications about her reactions in that event.

Given what we’ve seen from modern chapter 4 Yumi, I’m finding her early actions fascinating. Previously, I didn’t think she was actually tsundere, and that she actually did want to be left alone. Now, I’m not so sure.
