Uh oh, here comes Maya!
Hmm? Just gonna silently wait? What does that mean...?
And she ran away. Only time will tell what that kiss made her think.
Why is he going back to the party when Maya was suppose to be waiting at the rooftop? Is he stupid?
That voice fits Yasu really well. About as frail and mild and broken as she appears.
It's a scene like this that makes me realize how much content the dev could setup that makes her seem like she's enduring immeasurable pain to keep the world from breaking or something. You get what I mean? That slow singing, alone in a room, the way she dresses and everything else about her. Maybe she's not creepy, she's just misunderstood and acts the way she does to cope or something? I dunno. I just imagine like a scene where she has to face her demons and can't stop crying screaming and the mc just stands there in shock not knowing what to do. As if in that moment, she needs more comforting than any other character ever has. What a thought provoking scene this is. Maybe I'm getting ahead of myself.
If there is a firework show going on right now and Maya is on the roof... Hmmm...
Like for all I know, Yasu is just as normal as anyone else. Pain, suffering, emotions, confidence issues. She just has to show them in this unique way.
Miku couldn't keep it in after all...
Yep, there we go. Nodoka got too drunk.
So many people suffering this event...
Rin and Otoha's relationship will never work out, as wonderful as it is the problem is Otoha's parents would never approve of it and Otoha can't commit to the relationship beyond making Rin feel loved but she backs out and chooses her parents when that security is threatened. This will never be a viable relationship unless she can get her parents to approve and even then it feels like it would only be a matter of time before it all comes crashing down.
Welp... I should have known their relationship would reach this unstable point the moment we found out her parents were strict, which was before she had even arrived at the school to begin with.
I'm starting to think Tsukasa secretly belongs in the same tier as Kirin.
Chika feels like she have been drunk in that room before but I don't recall very well. The only incident I can recall about her being drunk is when Touka and her were doing a strip tease.
WHYYYYYYYYYYYYYYYY! He fucking forgot the meeting with Maya! That idiot! God fucking damnit how do you forget something like that!?
Welp. Apparently Yasu can tell Maya is pacing around on the top floor waiting for him.
Oh would you look at that. The reset event includes the number of stairs. Totally not suspicious at all.
And of course he missed the fire works.
No I can't say I recall seeing a girl from a game or series holding her hand to the sky the moment the mc or someone shows up.
Wonder if we will ever find out just how much time Maya has really spent going through these cycles.
He didn't stand Maya up. That's not how that works. He already had a plan and told her he will show up after that.
That slow transition of her facial expression when he said he remembered something... I can't tell if it's just surprise or fear and surprise, or concern?
Maya must HATE that. Not being able to tell him about the past without him short circuiting but Noriko and Niki can tell him just fine.
...isn't that the mystery girl sitting up there? I almost missed her...
Damn, he forced a blush out of her by pointing out she really is in love with him.
And another blush when he said his always liked seeing her in the shrine maiden outfit... The day when Maya stops holding back and the world doesn't try to destroy him in the process will be a good day.
Molly gave him a shirt... Well alright then. I bet she asked Ami for his size or something. It's very... blue.
Christmas event over.
Otoha doesn't look happy and the ominous "pull the plug" event name doesn't help.
She makes it sound like the Christmas party was long ago but it was yesterday. Makes me wonder if the dev intended for people to be very confused about where to go and what to do until some weeks have past and they finally figure it out. Like it's literally the morning after the night the party was happening and she was with her parents at that time. So she wouldn't have had many hours talking to anyone else at that point.
Rin is really that mad? To think that someone who falls so easily can afford to be mad.
Six rocks and a lesbian. Now that sounds like an interesting tv series if it existed.
Who said him dating the students is a good idea? He does that, Otoha don't and between the two, Otoha seems more sane (for now).
Otoha and Niki look like they are the same age. Far from the truth tho.
Mc really be taking a phone call in the middle of Otoha's vocal class.
"Two octave pitch glide tactic" That sounds ridiculous, like a fucking music shooter or action game or something.
That's so much pressure... Imagine having to treat your entire audience like they are your girlfriend!
Guess Otoha didn't expect a hug from behind by Niki.
Niki is ruthless in vocal cord teaching.
I can already tell Nodoka will grow up to be a mad scientist. She's already there technically.
There is surprisingly little food out there that's grey as far as I can tell. But they do exist.
She's like an inch away from his face right now.
His finally getting a little closer to Otoha.
Gotta love how the game is foreshadowing Otoha's manic episode so hard.
It's a double date, but one of the relationships ended a long time ago and the other is treading dangerous waters.
Yep, it's fucking over. Rin and Otoha's relationship is doomed. She got over the parent thing, Rin let the threat from her parents to cut off the money slip, Niki offered to pay for it, Otoha went silent and Rin got hurt by it.
Rin is just being way too pushy with this in general. She shouldn't have to see someone's parents, I don't know why I've been taking Rin's side on this the entire time in text or whatever I've been doing but I really don't think anyone should let a relationship hang by a main thread like this and let meeting parents be the deciding factor if the relationship works or not. I don't understand the obsession and whatever media I've played seem to portray it as a huge fucking deal.
Well, it appears the ship that was sailing on dangerous oceans appear to have got a leak.
So Otoha IS embarrassed to be dating a girl.
Honestly it's fucking unreasonable for parents to expect their daughter to be dating a man when most of the men are in fucking space of all places. At that point you aren't mad she's dating a girl, you are mad she's dating AT ALL. FWIW, I have no problem with Selebus telling the story the way he wants to, reset events and all, and if I did I would simply not play the game. It's his story. Click to expand...
Oh boy, dipping my toes dangerously into negative subjects here... I'll try to be neutral and polite!

It's important to understand that most people engage with fiction in something of a self-centered way; the fiction exists for them (or their conception of what would be ideal), rather than for its own sake. It's intuitive for many many many people that they are more important than the book in their hand or the game they're playing, so any personal problem they have is a problem with the fiction. We see in video game discourse, for example, a lot of controversy over 'accessibility,' with many people being very insistent that every game needs a lot of accessibility options so that as many people as possible can engage with it. Someone may play a sound-centric game with no deaf accessibility options and feel this is a problem with the game, even though it's hardly a categorical imperative that any given fiction needs to accommodate any issues a user may have.

With this established, let's take a closer look at the history of the happy scene. As the story goes, people were skipping happy scenes due to feeling scared or uncomfortable during them. I think while reading through F95's old posts I also encountered masturbators (derogatory) skipping them since ttey were playing with their dicks in hand (why they announced this I do not know). The power of ren'py allows them to control the fiction and shape it to their preferences. Selebus does not want users doing this, however. So to remove 'agency' from the player, and to maximize his intended vision for the fiction, he put puzzle answers in happy scenes to specifically prevent those who skipped them from progressing.

On the one hand, it is intuitive to you that people should be fully engaging with the media they consume - to read every scene put before them. On the other hand, to others its intuitive that their agency being deprived is an objective flaw, and only an asshole would go out of their way to spite them in that way. That would be the key. It's not that Selebus has generically put content in happy scenes. It's that he did so specifically to impact the audience - specifically to spite those playing in ways he does not approve. If there is a cardinal sin a creator can commit in the eyes of the audience, it is invariably treating them with spite. It is a VERY rare individual who puts fiction above themselves - a very rare individual who engages fiction for anyone's sake but their own.

In a sense, this is why we sometimes see cope about how Selebus is producing bad puzzle content 'while trying to make something good' or 'for greed' - there is an almost obsessive compulsion to apply Hanlon's razor and attribute these matters to incompetence rather than malice, because an incompetent or greedy developer is cute and beneath the reader, while a malicious developer is simply an enemy. It's harder to resolve the internal cognitive dissonance for why a person you feel internal distaste for is capable of producing you love. As for how some people spend hundreds upon hundreds of posts casually blasting Selebus with cruel hate while loving the bulk of his art so much, and appreciating the fragility of the characters within - I don't know! People are mean. A perceived slight is all it takes for someone to become less than human in their eyes. Uh oh? Is that not neutral or polite? Ohononono I'm sorry my evil innards are surging up my lungs in the form of my own hateful words

Anyway, that's my take. Beware ye author that inconveniences the reader.

LoveRedHairedGirl said:
Okay, guys, I tried to do something in Koikatsu Studio.
View attachment 4461184
View attachment 4461185
View attachment 4461186
90% of the work done here is on their skirts, because they just don't give a fuck about gravity. So, I have to fix them manually. The poses are pre-made Koikatsu poses.
What I really want to do is understand how to use lighting and shadows, because most KK h-games have the worst lighting I've ever seen, except for Imani's winter outfit, which is way worse.
Click to expand...
The skirts should be effected by gravity unless you toggle on their FK posing option. Or if you just mean they glitch through their legs, in that case the longer skirts are kind of busted (I think they just don't have enough bones to interact with the collision meshes without slipping past limbs and causing clipping). The easiest way I could find to help with that is after you pose them You can mess with the weight sliders for the enabled skirt dynamic bones in the advanced KKPE menu until the side of the skirt that is clipping is no longer doing so. But that might not work for some poses. You can also try the collision options in the same menu which can help mostly for smaller clipping problems. These settings should also help with long hair clipping. There is also a skirt collision toggle in the animation status menu you might need to turn on. You might have to just use the manual skirt FK posing sometimes like I assume you are doing but that's kind of annoying and I would try avoid it at all costs.

There might be a better solution, because you have to reset and re tweak all the skirt/hair bones if you repose the character which is also kind of annoying. But less than redoing an FK pose for a skirt. I know very little about CharacterStudio so maybe there are moded skirts with more bones in them or something like that idk.

The way the lighting works is a bit strange as well and I find it hard to get it to not look flat and ugly, ILLUSION did some weird things with it for performance reasons I assume. All the default lights will only cast a silhouette shadow off of an invisible low Polly model inside the character model. You will have to use some of the mod lights if you want character shadows to be cast on the environment and even then they don't work on some of the maps for reason I have yet to work out. Also sometimes the silhouette shadow caster clips through the model and you can get weird looking shadows so you can go into the material editor for the character and untick enabled for "o_shadowcaster". The main thing I have seen it do is just give the shadows big ears which is probably not something anyone would ever notice so it might be a waste of time tbh.

There is also the stuff zuko said which should help. And to add to that you can blend together 2 shades with the "scene shade adjustment slider" in the colour adjustment section. Which I have found you will usually need to do for alot of the options in there. zmr_005_LUT32 is probably the best night/dark option for example and you can blend it with other ones to change the brightness, colour temp, etc. The depth of field option can also help a lot. I think the effect centres around the white plus circle thing that the camera rotates around. So you just put that on what you want to be in focus and then mess with the sliders for it to see if you want to use it or not.

If you are using the [ScrewThisNoise] repack you can press F1 and search for "screenshot manager", in there you can change the screenshot resolution, but if you make it too big it will crash. There is also a plugin that comes with that repack called KK_ExpressionControl, I don't remember if its installed by default but if not it will be in the optional mods folder and you can add it from there. I think the default key bind to bring it up is "L", it makes it a lot easier to do the facial expressions. You can save pre-sets in it and the options are named instead of just being numbers you have to remember.

Also is it just me or is character studio ridiculously counter intuitive to use. I have spent way to long trying to figure out how to do what I figured would be simple things only for it to completely melt my mind with how obtuse it is. Maybe all animation software is like that and its just because I have never used any before? But I get the impression from using it that even if that is the case ILLUSION still must have added some of the finest Japanese counter intuitive UIUX that they could come up with at the time.

The way the lighting works is a bit strange as well and I find it hard to get it to not look flat and ugly, ILLUSION did some weird things with it for performance reasons I assume. All the default lights will only cast a silhouette shadow off of an invisible low Polly model inside the character model. You will have to use some of the mod lights if you want character shadows to be cast on the environment and even then they don't work on some of the maps for reason I have yet to work out. Also sometimes the silhouette shadow caster clips through the model and you can get weird looking shadows so you can go into the material editor for the character and untick enabled for "o_shadowcaster". The main thing I have seen it do is just give the shadows big ears which is probably not something anyone would ever notice so it might be a waste of time tbh.
There is also the stuff zuko said which should help. And to add to that you can blend together 2 shades with the "scene shade adjustment slider" in the colour adjustment section. Which I have found you will usually need to do for alot of the options in there. zmr_005_LUT32 is probably the best night/dark option for example and you can blend it with other ones to change the brightness, colour temp, etc. The depth of field option can also help a lot. I think the effect centres around the white plus circle thing that the camera rotates around. So you just put that on what you want to be in focus and then mess with the sliders for it to see if you want to use it or not.
If you are using the [ScrewThisNoise] repack you can press F1 and search for "screenshot manager", in there you can change the screenshot resolution, but if you make it too big it will crash. There is also a plugin that comes with that repack called KK_ExpressionControl, I don't remember if its installed by default but if not it will be in the optional mods folder and you can add it from there. I think the default key bind to bring it up is "L", it makes it a lot easier to do the facial expressions. You can save pre-sets in it and the options are named instead of just being numbers you have to remember.
Also is it just me or is character studio ridiculously counter intuitive to use. I have spent way to long trying to figure out how to do what I figured would be simple things only for it to completely melt my mind with how obtuse it is. Maybe all animation software is like that and its just because I have never used any before? But I get the impression from using it that even if that is the case ILLUSION still must have added some of the finest Japanese counter intuitive UIUX that they could come up with at the time.

posts.content_html_raw:
What is happening to me? I think I get Otoha (????)

The following is a long analysis of an event that made me hate Otoha less, and even like Otoha more (?). Anyway, I don't mean to convince anyone, but I think I have a new perspective on her, that makes me even a bit sympathetic towards her character. Thought I'd share it is all.
Okay, so, there's a lot to this conversation and I'm not going to cover everything. I recommend you go watch it yourself, as she explains all the Rin and Niki stuff before this - and yeah, she's basically a fuck up. However, none of it was really malicious, it was just fucking things up. Does that excuse her? Well, no, but she's not looking for excuses either, even though she does recognize that she is at fault. She just wants to figure things out so that she starts sucking less in the future.

This is where she starts pitching it to Akira, that even though they are fucking up people's lives and their own, they can become less scummy.



I find this interesting because, yeah, Otoha hasn't faced a tenth of Akira's trauma, nor has she caused trauma comparable to what he did. That being said, the general perspective is valid. Akira has this mentality where he refuses to be anything other than his past, and yet what she's saying is that you can be something other than it too. Which, again, it's a very general and shallow presentation of it, but neither does Otoha know about his past, nor is she anything other than a teenager. What I mean is that, it could be Yuki pitching the same ideas, and through her words, we'd likely that it in a much more serious tone.



Again, I like that she can't properly convey these ideas because, as noted, she is a teenager. All she can do is try. And I admire that she is trying, and trying for him as well.



And that is, I think, what catches Akira's attention. The camaraderie of two fuck-ups trying to figure shit out. Does he want to fuck Otoha? Obviously. But there's something else. And I started to wonder if things wouldn't have been different if he was introduced to Otoha before he was introduced to Rin. Again, this doesn't excuse Otoha, but as she said, she's been going through all of this sort of alone - what if she could have talked and had Akira's support since the beginning?



See, this is why I mentioned the "since the beginning" thing. Because being their friend is what Akira pitched at the beginning of Chapter 1. Granted, at that point he didn't even know he was Akira, and it was more of a excuse not to work/to groom them than anything else. But, regardless of his intentions, that did lead to Rin becoming his daughter didn't it? I just thought that Otoha had this really unfortunate circumstance where she wasn't there. Even as the second floor girls get Akira, she sort of doesn't, because it's never Akira, it's either "the dude my soon-to-be/girlfriend liked/still likes" or "the dude banging the teacher I want to bang" - it takes fucking forever until she can finally be rid of all these barriers and just be his friend. And, honestly, I can finally pity her - because I can see how she would have benefited from this relationship much earlier.



And thus, they become siblings. The dynamic is finally set.



After this long ramble, it was this sentence that made me rethink the whole thing, and it's really heartwarming:



Then sibling energy reaches maximum output:



The throwing food at my head is such a sibling thing I can't even
Who knew I'd be writing such a post, right? The wonders of a replay. Well, maybe it's not impossible for Otoha to be redeemed. That's my takeaway.

However, none of it was really malicious, it was just fucking things up. Does that excuse her? Well, no, but she's not looking for excuses either, even though she does recognize that she is at fault. This is where she starts pitching it to Akira, that even though they are fucking up people's lives and their own, they can become less scummy.

Moonflare said:
What is happening to me? I think I get Otoha (????)

The following is a long analysis of an event that made me hate Otoha less, and even like Otoha more (?). Anyway, I don't mean to convince anyone, but I think I have a new perspective on her, that makes me even a bit sympathetic towards her character. Thought I'd share it is all.
Okay, so, there's a lot to this conversation and I'm not going to cover everything. I recommend you go watch it yourself, as she explains all the Rin and Niki stuff before this - and yeah, she's basically a fuck up. However, none of it was really malicious, it was just fucking things up. Does that excuse her? Well, no, but she's not looking for excuses either, even though she does recognize that she is at fault. She just wants to figure things out so that she starts sucking less in the future.

This is where she starts pitching it to Akira, that even though they are fucking up people's lives and their own, they can become less scummy.

View attachment 4465528 View attachment 4465532

I find this interesting because, yeah, Otoha hasn't faced a tenth of Akira's trauma, nor has she caused trauma comparable to what he did. That being said, the general perspective is valid. Akira has this mentality where he refuses to be anything other than his past, and yet what she's saying is that you can be something other than it too. Which, again, it's a very general and shallow presentation of it, but neither does Otoha know about his past, nor is she anything other than a teenager. What I mean is that, it could be Yuki pitching the same ideas, and through her words, we'd likely that it in a much more serious tone.

View attachment 4465533 View attachment 4465536

Again, I like that she can't properly convey these ideas because, as noted, she is a teenager. All she can do is try. And I admire that she is trying, and trying for him as well.

View attachment 4465537 View attachment 4465538

And that is, I think, what catches Akira's attention. The camaraderie of two fuck-ups trying to figure shit out. Does he want to fuck Otoha? Obviously. But there's something else. And I started to wonder if things wouldn't have been different if he was introduced to Otoha before he was introduced to Rin. Again, this doesn't excuse Otoha, but as she said, she's been going through all of this sort of alone - what if she could have talked and had Akira's support since the beginning?

View attachment 4465541 View attachment 4465543 View attachment 4465546 View attachment 4465547

See, this is why I mentioned the "since the beginning" thing. Because being their friend is what Akira pitched at the beginning of Chapter 1. Granted, at that point he didn't even know he was Akira, and it was more of a excuse not to work/to groom them than anything else. But, regardless of his intentions, that did lead to Rin becoming his daughter didn't it? I just thought that Otoha had this really unfortunate circumstance where she wasn't there. Even as the second floor girls get Akira, she sort of doesn't, because it's never Akira, it's either "the dude my soon-to-be/girlfriend liked/still likes" or "the dude banging the teacher I want to bang" - it takes fucking forever until she can finally be rid of all these barriers and just be his friend. And, honestly, I can finally pity her - because I can see how she would have benefited from this relationship much earlier.

View attachment 4465550

And thus, they become siblings. The dynamic is finally set.

View attachment 4465551

After this long ramble, it was this sentence that made me rethink the whole thing, and it's really heartwarming:

View attachment 4465552

Then sibling energy reaches maximum output:

View attachment 4465553

The throwing food at my head is such a sibling thing I can't even
Who knew I'd be writing such a post, right? The wonders of a replay. Well, maybe it's not impossible for Otoha to be redeemed. That's my takeaway.

I recommend you go watch it yourself, as she explains all the Rin and Niki stuff before this - and yeah, she's basically a fuck up. However, none of it was really malicious, it was just fucking things up. Does that excuse her? Well, no, but she's not looking for excuses either, even though she does recognize that she is at fault. Akira has this mentality where he refuses to be anything other than his past, and yet what she's saying is that you can be something other than it too. Which, again, it's a very general and shallow presentation of it, but neither does Otoha know about his past, nor is she anything other than a teenager. What I mean is that, it could be Yuki pitching the same ideas, and through her words, we'd likely that it in a much more serious tone.

Update 0.46 came with an early birthday present for Tsukasa: lifelong trauma. I decided to do a detailed write-up of what's happening with her because I think it needs to be stressed just how suuuuuuper fucked up these scenes are on the green path. In particular:
  • In the ending of "A Part of Your World" Sensei is knowingly grooming Tsukasa, even if he also genuinely want to make her feel better.
  • For Tsubasa, getting Sensei off and her own sadistic pleasure are both secondary to her real goal in "Yes, Mother". She's using his mommy kink as a tool to make him relive his trauma so that she can manipulate him.
  • Because of Tsubasa's manipulation, Sensei abandons any remaining pretensions to protect Tsukasa. Now he wants to recreate his own trauma and become Tsukasa's Sekai. He wants to make her just as broken as he is.
I saw several people praise the interaction between Sensei and Tsukasa as wholesome, but I think with context it's much darker than that - he's engaging in classic grooming behavior.

After Touka is inadvertently cruel to Tsukasa, he makes her leave before she can apologize and emphasizes that even if Tsukasa's family doesn't want her, he does.

Here's the second half of the post.
(This interaction can't be seen on replay because the flag check happens before URM can be invoked.)

After pushing Sensei towards Tsukasa, Tsubasa runs into Tsukasa and pushes her towards Sensei. This is supposedly a chance encounter, but I have my doubts; earlier she emphasized that she knows everything that happens in the manor and Tsukasa left the party even before Sensei did.
Tsubasa is intentionally alienating Tsukasa from herself in this scene. She tells Tsukasa that she's wanted, but implies it's only because she's useful, and then immediately sends her to her room, reinforcing Tsukasa's belief that her mother doesn't want her around. It would be very easy to offer Tsukasa just a bit of love and reassurance here, but instead she denigrates her and pushes her away.
I take Tsubasa's reaction after Tsukasa leaves to mean that she doesn't enjoy what she just did.
After all, she does seem to care for Tsukasa, based on her previous response to Sensei pointing out her neglect (especially the swimming pool scene with her daughters).

I think the fact that she does all this despite finding it distasteful actually makes her actions even worse. She's trying to accomplish something by neglecting Tsukasa and pushing her toward Sensei. I don't see any interpretation other than she wants her daughter to be abused because it furthers some goal.
After the Tsubasa scene, Sensei's attitude toward Tsukasa changes markedly. Technically, I think this change always happens on the Tsukasa path, regardless of whether you meet the lust requirements to see Tsubasa's scene. I'm chalking this up to either oversight from Sel or just another case of a non-green path being inconsistent.

He no longer cares about protecting her, instead he fully embraces his own depravity and decides that he's going to become Tsukasa's Sekai. He doesn't even delude himself that this will be positive for her; he wants to break her. This is all revealed when he brings Imani to Tsukasa's room to fuck her.
Sensei has been reminded he's a predator just like Sekai, so he's going to traumatize Tsukasa and haunt her in the future the same way Sekai haunts him.
He's making Imani roleplay the role of a disobedient brat, so that he can pretend he's "correcting" Tsukasa.
His new desire to break Tsukasa comes from trying to forget/minimize his own trauma after Tsubasa dredged it back up.
We can hope that these feelings were temporary because of Sensei's poor mental state and trauma-induced vulnerability, but I'm not optimistic. We've been shown the way that this "relationship" will inevitably progress.

I'm guessing this will be an unpopular opinion, but for me this event is more upsetting than "Stomachache" was. This is the prelude to abuse rather than the abuse itself, but all the context around the event and especially Sensei's thoughts and intentions are so much worse.

In "Stomachache" Sensei deludes himself into thinking he can help Io by showing her his "love", and starts to break down when he realizes that he can't make her enjoy it. He's trying to fix a broken person but doesn't know how because he's broken himself. While Io obviously didn't deserve what happened to her, she did offer herself to Sensei and egg him on. There was no false pretenses around their relationship; Io hoped she could keep sex out of it, but she knew from the start that Sensei wanted it.

In contrast, Sensei doesn't give a rat's ass about helping Tsukasa. He doesn't want to show her love, he wants to show her the illusion of it. Rather than trying to fix a broken person, he wants to break an innocent girl. Tsukasa has done nothing to ask for this, but she's being dragged into it anyway by her tutor and her own mother. And on top of everything else, he's using Imani as an unwitting sex object while he actually gets off by thinking about abusing a wizard.
She's the devil incarnate.

OK, not really, she's more like what would happen if Nodoka had access to infinite resources. She wants to replace a missing god and make a better world, but she's prepared to take any steps necessary to get there, no matter how abhorrent.

I think people are right that the secret Christmas meeting was about an arranged marriage for Tsukasa, and that's what forced her to accelerate her plans and practically throw Tsukasa at Sensei before the situation changes. That's not the underlying motive, though; she has always intended for Sensei to break both of her daughters, despite her protestations to the contrary.

She doesn't like being cruel to Tsukasa, but does it anyway. I don't think this is because anyone/anything is forcing her to do it, but rather she feels that it's necessary to hurt the family that she cares about in pursuit of the greater good. Tsukasa is a daughter that she loves, but that's less important than her usefulness as a tool.

I'm still not entirely sure what her end goal is or how sacrificing Tsukasa helps her get closer, but I will remind everyone that there is a narrator who is either Tsubasa or someone closely linked to her, and that particular narrator seems to be a fan of the Pareidolia/Sekai strategy of "break the girls in order to rebuild them". Getting Sensei to embrace his darkest instincts might be the push he needs to really turn into the Collector.

spoilers.title: A Part of Your World
spoilers.html:
I saw several people praise the interaction between Sensei and Tsukasa as wholesome, but I think with context it's much darker than that - he's engaging in classic grooming behavior.

After Touka is inadvertently cruel to Tsukasa, he makes her leave before she can apologize and emphasizes that even if Tsukasa's family doesn't want her, he does.
View attachment 4466025 View attachment 4466026
He tells her that he's going out his way to help her, which has the intended effect of making her feel grateful for the attention. It also primes her to think that he's doing her a favor so she owes him.
View attachment 4466028 View attachment 4466029 View attachment 4466030 View attachment 4466031
...
View attachment 4466033
He thinks of her as his pupil with special emphasis, which has disturbing connotations given what he's done with past pupils and how he connects this thought with the idea that he needs to be watched around her.
View attachment 4466027
He's doing this because he knows what it's like to be her. This has both a positive and a negative meaning. Positive in that he remembers feeling unwanted as a child and wants to give her the attention/affection she's missing. Negative in that he remembers being groomed himself, and he's repeating the cycle.

I think at this point Sensei has still convinced himself he has good intentions. He does genuinely empathize with her and wants to make her feel better. He could have taken further advantage of the situation to drive a wedge between Tsukasa and Touka, but instead he make attempts to explain what Touka said and apologize for her. On the other hand, he knows the effect of what he's doing; he knows he now has Tsukasa eating out of the palm of his hand and could easily take advantage of her. That's why he's in hell seeing her happy because of him.

posts.content_html_raw:
Day 40 character count 10060.
Hmm? Did Maya or the world(God?) erase Ayane's memory of the boxes? Given how interesting those were even to Ayane, I can't even imagine what could be in there.

Damn dude, I guess Maya isn't used to being told to stop. Bet she wishes Ayane never appears on that rooftop that one day.
I think Maya is a bit grumpy now not being allowed to talk to them.

WOW DUDE! Just gonna go and assume a favor Wakana is asking related to estrogen means she wants you to fuck her girlfriend, huh?

So both Osako and Wakana are 28.

They can wear whatever they want? Did they loosen the dress code? Convenient.

Yumi finding out about the dress code changes then joking that Chika is gonna tell her about another thing that's gonna ruin her school life, which conveniently happens to be the mandatory club assignment.

I still don't understand how the richest family in Kumon-mi isn't allowed to come and go as they please.

remember to smile, for if you don't- you get jumpscared?

Ami reading Tsuneyo's mind. "Noodles."

Rin's whole vibe has changed because of that hairstyle. I think I think she's cuter but I'm not sure nor am I sure there is some other underlying emotion.
What I can say however is that she has now separated her haircut from resembling Chika's. Only a matter of time before it stops resembling Otoha's too which is a thing I think I know is going to happen.

I see two uncomfortable friends about to talk about something difficult caused by Molly's awkward approach to love. I still don't know how that talk is going to be or what it will be about beyond trying to repair the friendship.

And seriously, Rin is like a whole new person with that haircut and outfit... If Rin had a sister, that's probably how she would look.

No, Molly. It's worse to ignore someone's feelings than it is to not understand them. The former is a conscious decision to be cruel, the latter is no decision at all.

I don't think I would call Tsuneyo cool... Chill, maybe. But not the kind of cool that wears sunglasses, don't look at explosions and so on.

Oh, Molly noticed the shirt!

The mc forgot about being the manga club advisor. Completely forgot. Or the dev somehow forgot he had already put that in.

Damnit mc! You should have told Imani not to mention Wakana is the advisor for the archery club! This is such a typical mc slip up, like seriously. He really doesn't care at the end of the day.

Damn dude, Imani is savage to Makoto! "Page 1! section A! if your name is Makoto, shut up!"

Called it. Sana joining the music group.

Otoha worrying about a sort of love triangle situation? Can't really see any other reason since Sana was allowed to join with no experience with drums.

Damnit Io! It's one word!

Imani already knows how Nodoka works. Super genius who undresses people with her eyes and doesn't have the courage to make a move.

Yumi? Swim club? WHAT? Mighty brave choosing the swim club over archery. I guess it sort of IS the most fitting one for her since she doesn't do music, is probably not into weeb shit... wait, doesn't she have a manga closet of some sort... Even if that were the case, I imagine she wouldn't want to associate with other people like that and might find it embarrassing? And uhh, I guess archery might be too inactive and she probably has some excuse against it. Given how physically developed she is and likely strong, enjoying the beach, swimming fits. There is the concern about the mc visiting the them which you know he will and you know he will see Yumi and she will freak out about it, that is pretty obvious. Question is how badly she will freak out about it and if she will regret joining the club or if on account of being tsundere, she somehow hopes that will or don't mind it nearly as much. I dunno.

Yasu joining the manga club is definitely unusual but you know it somehow fits surprisingly well. Molly confuses her rants for games, Ami and Futaba are welcoming, Futaba is patient, Ami won't mind on account of Yasu not being into the mc (yet). Maya on the other hand... hmmm. Can an ultra believer like Yasu and someone like Maya who hates god but is involved in religious bullshit anyway get along? I don't think so. Which is why this could turn out funny.
Yasu is too weak for both swimming and archery and the music club's vibe is the opposite of hers... unless they went for some kind of baby metal religious rock sort of thing, but nah. By process of elimination, the manga club is the only one fitting for her. Oh yeah, also cosplay. She did participate in that gothic dressup.
Damn... It didn't take long for Maya to prove me right. She doesn't want this religious fanatic in the club at all. She also did just say she would rather read in the dorms. But her reason was because they keep calling her a nerd on the board...

Reaching freeroam sure took a while. And to think that 2 days ago I thought I could somehow get the pre-reset, happy event, reset and whatever comes after until freeroam done in just like 2 hours... Yeah, I went to sleep early, played the entire day, went to sleep late at 6 am and have felt the lack of energy today and I just now at 8:40 pm manages to reach freeroam. Crazy.

Oh, I unlocked more areas! Fun.
Oh that's a lot of potential interactions. If there's at least one unique repeatable dialogue, it could potentially be another 23 to see.

Had my first proper test at archery not so long ago. Proper draw-weights, some weight to the bow although I don't remember. Some training on how to stand and such. It's not as easy as it may seem even doing it indoors. Any micro movements can throw off the 5-10 meter away target precision by quite a bit, more than enough to miss a target. I would do that again if I had easy access to it. Used those handguard things and if you are not careful and hit your arm with the string, oof that will sting and you will feel it for a little while. Those strings are not to be messed with. They could probably be used a weapon by themselves if angles correctly and the opponent is dumb and slow enough.

Given how Yasu have expressed the ability of foresight, it's not too hard to believe that she knew he would show up on this day needing the remaining seat which was left unoccupied by the rabbits.

Yasu's already wide creepy smile gets even wider. Stop that.
And now what is that expression? This down the rabbit hole event doesn't help make Yasu seem like less of a religious fanatic.
She definitely has the ability to trigger these blackouts of his. If it weren't for the fact he has those, I might actually be freaked out by her sudden disappearance.

Ami's poor phone getting yeeted across the room... cat videos are dangerous.

Yasu has(had?) amnesia, probably.

I wonder what the percentage is of manga that lacks any physical violence, sex and physical romance that's popular enough for me to recognize? And I guess doesn't cover any topics that religion might not like.

It's weird that chapter 3 starts of with nothing but Yasu events after the first few main.

Have the owners come by declare the church abandoned and lock it up or something?

I really hope I'm not wrong about this but I can tell right now that that door is not opening for her again and that this is necessary for character development. She is far too invested in this religion of hers and I think whatever god like entity may or may not be watching over the world sees her destroying herself in delusions and forced this change to take place so that she will adapt to life and try to become a "normal" girl. If this is the direction Yasu's path is taking, I may get convinced to like this girl and admire her cute moments. Would an entire 10 chapters work if she was still obsessing over the church and her beliefs? I think I'm talking too soon but I think most of us can agree that it's hard to fall for a girl who pays more attention to her religion than the wonders of life in her delusions of some greater being. I doubt she will just forget about the religion, but she should at least slow down a bit and try to be a normal girl.

But really, if you were some god like entity and some girl wasted away her precious life dedicating it to you and you can't do much in return to her, what would you do? Would you let her continue in her delusions or try to push her to live a better life? This really is no different than spending like 6 hours on the computer to spending 12 hours. The former is a mild addiction that still allows you to live your life and the latter is a dangerous one(speaking from experience as you know). If there is some god out there, don't you think they would have tried to destroy my computer and have someone show up offering me a wonderful opportunity to get back into society? I think they would. Alas, I am not that fortunate but at least Yasu is.

Wonder if the reason Yasu's events are appearing first is to push her in the direction of falling in line with the other characters so the player can start to see her differently and she will be more open to participation knowing she can't spend time at the church the way she used to. Did anyone see this outcome coming with her being locked out of an abandoned church? I didn't, but in hindsight it makes sense.

Despite everything that's happened so far, I think the game has never told you that the things Yasu believes in are false. But I feel like locking the most religious character out of her place of worship in a game certainly speaks volume for her fake her religion really is. But I can't quite figure out why this god of her would stop communicating with her. Is that really something she has made up? I don't know how it all works. The door was locked causing Yasu's subconscious side make her conscious side believe that the god no longer speaks to her? Honestly, anything can happen with Yasu at this point.

Gosh her eyes as huge!

Well, you can still find her in the cathedral so it might not be closed for good. Or this is just some detail the dev didn't bother with. But he did bother with Yumi's broken phone which magically got repaired again.
Honestly I have little reason to dislike Nodoka. She just seems like one of those characters you are meant to like.

There is the concern about the mc visiting the them which you know he will and you know he will see Yumi and she will freak out about it, that is pretty obvious. Question is how badly she will freak out about it and if she will regret joining the club or if on account of being tsundere, she somehow hopes that will or don't mind it nearly as much. I dunno.
Yasu joining the manga club is definitely unusual but you know it somehow fits surprisingly well. Molly confuses her rants for games, Ami and Futaba are welcoming, Futaba is patient, Ami won't mind on account of Yasu not being into the mc (yet). Maya on the other hand... hmmm. Can an ultra believer like Yasu and someone like Maya who hates god but is involved in religious bullshit anyway get along? I don't think so. Which is why this could turn out funny.
Yasu is too weak for both swimming and archery and the music club's vibe is the opposite of hers... unless they went for some kind of baby metal religious rock sort of thing, but nah. By process of elimination, the manga club is the only one fitting for her. Oh yeah, also cosplay. She did participate in that gothic dressup.
Damn... It didn't take long for Maya to prove me right. She doesn't want this religious fanatic in the club at all. She also did just say she would rather read in the dorms. But her reason was because they keep calling her a nerd on the board...
Reaching freeroam sure took a while. And to think that 2 days ago I thought I could somehow get the pre-reset, happy event, reset and whatever comes after until freeroam done in just like 2 hours... Yeah, I went to sleep early, played the entire day, went to sleep late at 6 am and have felt the lack of energy today and I just now at 8:40 pm manages to reach freeroam. Crazy.
Oh, I unlocked more areas! Fun.
Oh that's a lot of potential interactions. If there's at least one unique repeatable dialogue, it could potentially be another 23 to see.
Had my first proper test at archery not so long ago. Proper draw-weights, some weight to the bow although I don't remember. Some training on how to stand and such. It's not as easy as it may seem even doing it indoors. Any micro movements can throw off the 5-10 meter away target precision by quite a bit, more than enough to miss a target. I would do that again if I had easy access to it. Used those handguard things and if you are not careful and hit your arm with the string, oof that will sting and you will feel it for a little while. Those strings are not to be messed with. They could probably be used a weapon by themselves if angles correctly and the opponent is dumb and slow enough.
Given how Yasu have expressed the ability of foresight, it's not too hard to believe that she knew he would show up on this day needing the remaining seat which was left unoccupied by the rabbits.
Yasu's already wide creepy smile gets even wider. Stop that.
And now what is that expression? This down the rabbit hole event doesn't help make Yasu seem like less of a religious fanatic.
She definitely has the ability to trigger these blackouts of his. If it weren't for the fact he has those, I might actually be freaked out by her sudden disappearance.
Ami's poor phone getting yeeted across the room... cat videos are dangerous.
Yasu has(had?) amnesia, probably.
I wonder what the percentage is of manga that lacks any physical violence, sex and physical romance that's popular enough for me to recognize? And I guess doesn't cover any topics that religion might not like.
It's weird that chapter 3 starts of with nothing but Yasu events after the first few main.
Have the owners come by declare the church abandoned and lock it up or something?
I really hope I'm not wrong about this but I can tell right now that that door is not opening for her again and that this is necessary for character development. She is far too invested in this religion of hers and I think whatever god like entity may or may not be watching over the world sees her destroying herself in delusions and forced this change to take place so that she will adapt to life and try to become a "normal" girl. If this is the direction Yasu's path is taking, I may get convinced to like this girl and admire her cute moments. Would an entire 10 chapters work if she was still obsessing over the church and her beliefs? I think I'm talking too soon but I think most of us can agree that it's hard to fall for a girl who pays more attention to her religion than the wonders of life in her delusions of some greater being. I doubt she will just forget about the religion, but she should at least slow down a bit and try to be a normal girl.
But really, if you were some god like entity and some girl wasted away her precious life dedicating it to you and you can't do much in return to her, what would you do? Would you let her continue in her delusions or try to push her to live a better life? This really is no different than spending like 6 hours on the computer to spending 12 hours. The former is a mild addiction that still allows you to live your life and the latter is a dangerous one(speaking from experience as you know). If there is some god out there, don't you think they would have tried to destroy my computer and have someone show up offering me a wonderful opportunity to get back into society? I think they would. Alas, I am not that fortunate but at least Yasu is.
Wonder if the reason Yasu's events are appearing first is to push her in the direction of falling in line with the other characters so the player can start to see her differently and she will be more open to participation knowing she can't spend time at the church the way she used to. Did anyone see this outcome coming with her being locked out of an abandoned church? I didn't, but in hindsight it makes sense.
Despite everything that's happened so far, I think the game has never told you that the things Yasu believes in are false. But I feel like locking the most religious character out of her place of worship in a game certainly speaks volume for her fake her religion really is. But I can't quite figure out why this god of her would stop communicating with her. Is that really something she has made up? I don't know how it all works. The door was locked causing Yasu's subconscious side make her conscious side believe that the god no longer speaks to her? Honestly, anything can happen with Yasu at this point.
Gosh her eyes as huge!
Well, you can still find her in the cathedral so it might not be closed for good. Or this is just some detail the dev didn't bother with. But he did bother with Yumi's broken phone which magically got repaired again.

Honestly I have little reason to dislike Nodoka. She just seems like one of those characters you are meant to like.

On the unlikely offchance someone doesn't understand the reference here:
This is a famous scene from Fate/Stay Night (A visual novel), which has been redone a million times inside and out of the series.


The context for the scene is that Shirou Emiya, a highschool student and mediocre mage, ends up as a target for elimination during a Holy Grail War (a war between mages and their summoned servants), because of his potential to become one of the competitors. However, he accidentally ends up summoning a servant in the middle of being attacked, and the summoned spirit (referred to by their battle class "Saber", even though their real identity is Arthur Pendragon, the mythical King of England). This scene is their first meeting upon summoning, in which Saber asks him if he is her master.
I can't really see a parallel between the scenes other than aesthetics however. Nao-chan doesn't seem to be in Akira's service, and neither does Akira seem to be one of the competitors in a (divine) war.

Should I try this?
Click to expand...
I mean, it's definitely one of the classics that spawned a whole genre.
The original Fate/Stay Night is a story with three main "routes", that you're supposed to see in order. Those being "Fate", "Unlimited Blade Works" and "Heaven's Feel", in that order.

Within those routes there are some choices, that mostly lead to bad ends. Although there are some variations at the end of each one between "good" and "normal" endings too. So, when you manage to complete the first route, you're supposed to restart the game and now you'll be able to make a different choice in the first chapters which will lead to the second route. And the same with the third after finishing the second. Each of them has a divergent point in the beginning of the game, so it's debatably a new game/timeline with the same characters from that point on.

The point of all of this is that with each route, your understanding of what was going on behind the scenes increases, and it becomes increasingly tragic as well. If playing, I advise to follow a guide. Each route also has a specific love interest, those being


1. Saber (blonde) - Fate Route
2. Rin (black hair) - Unlimited Blade Works Route
3. Sakura (purple hair) - Heaven's Feel Route

The first one is pretty safe/lovey dovey, it plays on the theme of idealism. The second one starts to get darker because it's a challenge to those very themes. Then the third one exposes everything that was going on and yet the player had no idea about in the background. The protagonist will always be Shirou Emiya, a teenager with a hero complex born out of survivor's guilt. The way he deal with it also changes in each of the routes.

Anyway, there is a lot to say about the game, I recommend anyone to play it as it is a classic. Tsukihime is also a good one by the same author (my avatar is one of the heroines), but Fate has an official English translation now and it is far more influential.

posts.content_html_raw:
With a week to go to the next LiL update, there is no better time to make good on my promise to analyze the writing changes to Lessons in Love brought about by the rework done a couple of years ago. To begin this comparison I would like to begin with a bit of an superfluous lecture: it is my near-universal experience that writers simply do not improve over time despite the common intuition being that people will improve at their craft over time. It really, really doesm ake sense that the more one writes the better one would get at writing, and therefore that we can anticipate writers improving. In general, though, I have found that not to be the case whatsoever. Most common examples of this are actually, by my judgement, misunderstandings of a completely separate phenomenon: that our evaluation of media improves the more time we spend with it. This is to say, we will have a harsher evaluation of Volume 1 of a book as it introduces characters and brings us into the world than we will on Volume 10 of a book where we are fully integrated into the story and all the gears are turning. I think people will often mistake this momentum for an improvement in writing quality when, in reality, the writing has not changed, only their perception of it. (More shallowly, a lot of people are barely capable of analyzing/parsing prose itself, and tend to associate e.g. improved visuals and music with improved writing somehow, as if a scene looking and sounding better suddenly makes the writing better too).

As for the writing itself divorced of all other factors, well, I have almost universally seen that authors simply do not improve notably over time. A genius will tend to demonstrate their innate talent in the first work they ever produce, such that even after decades of reading their work one can comfortably enjoy their debut work: Goethe stepped into fiction with The Sorrows of Young Werther and began composing Faust Part One in 1772 (see: the Urfaust); Gene Wolfe produced The Fifth Head of fucking Cerberus in 1972 and proceeded in swift order to release the Book of the New Sun, widely regarded as the greatest work of modern science fiction; I need not mention Tolkien; Dostoevsky began his rich career with the widely lauded Poor Folk; etc. Inversely, someone who produces shitty early work will probably never improve all that much (and I will spare the flame war which may arise by my listing of examples of poor authors).

In every case where I have read a series and felt that the writing quality has improved significantly, I've checked the credits and found that in reality a new writer was hired or something of the like. Every time I've followed an author for a long time, I've found their quality to be fairly stable with the usual peaks and valleys of chance resonance; even following long-term fantasy series, for example, I rarely judge that an author has improved after the 3 millionth word of prose despite the fact you would really expect that much quantity to have made a difference. And yet, it almost never does; a good author may may get a bit better, but a shitty author or mediocre author almost never raise to greatness. Of course, I am but one man and I have certainly not read every single author to ever live, so I can speak only of a trend as I see it.

This now brings us to Lessons in Love: a very rare (in my experience) exception to this. Selebus did in fact improve as an author, and somewhat dramatically; I find this pretty remarkable and believe that this transformation would be well-worth studying for any would-be writer who finds themselves insecure about their prose. We can use Selebus's modifications of his own writing in the past to glean insights into what techniques are more successful than others. For the purpose of this comparison I will be using a copy of 0.23 that I grabbed from I believe the subscribestar, since it was the last version before the rework. For convenience I shall distinguish them as "LiL 0" and "Neo LiL."

However, before I begin, I must make one more superfluous aside: despite being rich with insight itself, I will take the liberty of skipping the opening of LiL 0. It is by far Selebus's greatest embarrassment and I would not like to shine a spotlight on it specifically after he took such great pains to purge it from the game. That's not to say that this entire endeavor of mine is not similarly a slap to the rework's face, but for dramatic effect I will skip the opening regardless; my malice is not so limitless.

Okay, and without further ado, let us finally begin!

An early example of improved writing would be in the first conversation with Ami, when Sensei forgets her name. (For the purposes of this comparison I will take what is stated at face value and not speculate on, e.g., the fact Ami is almost certainly not actually surprised Sensei doesn't remember her name.)


In the original Ami noticing this and introducing her name is a very bland exchange which completes the function of introducing her name swiftly but without much personality. In the rework, it occurs in a much more interesting way: first, "how can you just forget that we've been living together for years" is very natural exposition phrased as a question. Second, "what's next, are you going to tell me youve forgotten my name" plays into the dramatic irony that we the player know Sensei has forgotten her name and in fact her name is ??? as she states this. The pause as Sensei waffles on whether to be honest on this is an early insight into his personality, and then Ami's freakout afterwards is humorous (especially with the visual of her shocked face). To finish matters off with aplomb, Sensei says it's not personal - "probably," prompting another shocked reaction from Ami.

Now, I think the improvement in writing quality is pretty obvious, but since this is a rare subject to be discussed I will belabor the point a bit. The original is wholly unremarkable and almost entirely lacking in humor or character development: it's not actively bad in a way which will earn ire, but it also does nothing good, either, and there is no worse fate for writing than to be completely boring. The rework, however, excels in all areas and manages to tell like 4 jokes in rapid-fire succession. There's a rather popular video that contrasts the old Simpsons with modern Simpsons: https://youtu.be/KqFNbCcyFkk?t=517 . The example used is how in Old Simpsons, a joke was never just a one-off; the jokes would have layers, and a funny sequence would build on itself 4-5 twists of expectations, instead of just being a joke and done. We can sort of apply this lens here; in LiL, the original text here... well... wasn't even trying to tell a joke, while the rewrite has humor exuding from every line.

Although I will be only providing a limited number of examples in this post, it's valuable to keep in mind that transformations like the above have taken place all over the narration of the original. Swathes of previously bland, "lazy" even narration is transformed into sequences of multi-layered and original humor. I simply can't cover each one (for example, how superior the introduction of the space war is).

But the improvements were not just in humor. Let us gaze up on example 2.


Again, most people with eyes will be able to distinguish the quality here, but I will belabor the point regardless.

It is here that I must invoke that most dreaded concept in writing criticism: show not tell. This is a concept INCREDIBLY misused by the populace at large and tends to be wielded like a club to criticize a work whenever a reader feels it is being boring in some way. The thing is that 'show' and 'tell' are vague enough words that one can apply them to almost anything: that is to say, someone can accuse anything they want to be 'telling' instead of 'showing' without leaving much room for argument. It is for this reason that 'show not tell' must be invoked with extreme care and a consideration for Chekhov's original purpose in bringing it.

And that purpose was to place greater emphasis on details rather than what the details are describing. Rather than say 'the moon is shining,' describe 'a glint of moonlight on broken glass' so that the reader can infer the moon is shining in a more evocative way. We can say (and this is of course my personal interpretation - there is no singular way of interpreting aesthetic rules in literature) that a reader will tend to feel greater satisfaction and immersion when they are putting many details together to form a whole in their mind rather than simply having the whole thrust into their face, and this Ami quote embodies this extremely well.

In LiL 0, despite how the scene seems to avoid a direct description, we are in reality clubbed over the head that Ami is disturbed by the question about her parents. A wordy, verbose passage descriptions all the various actions she takes, going to such extraordinary lengths as to describe her panicked breaths and wobbly knees. The moment is punctuated by a weak, "Um... Could you maybe ask something else instead?"

In this moment I would suggest there is zero drama or intrigue. We can feel the author telling us to be intrigued, telling us there is drama here... and because it is so obvious, we lose interest; there is nothing really for us to imagine or ponder. Ami herself becomes increasingly a bit of a pathetic figure as she weakly asks him to change his question. (again: not speculating as to whether this is all an act at this moment in time). The idea of alluding to Ami's trauma and the accident with her parents is clear, but executed extremely amateurly.

Neo LiL's superior execution is hardly a question. First, Ami cuts him off before he can even finish speaking, establishing her STRONG AURA. Second, she s simply says 'ask something else," giving no allusion to how she is feeling or what she is thinking behind her mask. When Sensei protests, she again cuts him off and demands he ask something else with no change in her smiling expression.

This is great. THIS is intrigue. We are being 'shown' the detail of her refusing to answer, and from this we start to paint the bigger picture in her mind. The initial characterization of Ami being kind of weak and lame was not strong, but already in Neo LiL one will be starting to sense Ami's latent psychopathy and the damage left by certain events. This dialogue is so good that Sensei (probably deliberately but maybe not) repeated it in a later scene with Wakana and Sensei, where Wakana references 'the jaws of life' and Sensei obstinately says "Choose another metaphor." This is how you get an audience intrigued in characters and wanting to learn more.

Another subtle detail is that he has universally excised bits of narration which imply significant passage of time. For example, the narration says she "focuses for a long time on the distant horizon," but this is completely dissonant with the act of reading the visual novel; we ourselves click through this line in matter of 1 second, and don't see any such deliberation from her, so immersion is hurt. It is a reflection of gained wisdom that Selebus knew to cut these out and in future narration pay greater effort to aligning the reading experience with the reality described in the text.

Now, I will take a brief aside to look at something which is not strictly prose but may be interesting to mention in part.


In LiL 0, after looking at the book of students, the scene ends briskly and cuts to Ami in a bath. In Neo LiL, we find her leaning over Sensei's shoulder ominously. This isn't a matter of prose but in scenes like this we can see a matured ability to simulate the actions of characters and juggle multiple concepts at once; the scene goes from a simple "go to room -> look at journal -> put journal down" to a multifaceted "go to room -> look at journal -> Ami was there the whole time -> interaction between two characters" (blah blah). Macro improvements are less interesting in general though (since they're more obvious) so I'll leave it at that.

Anyway, moving on, let us look at the following examples of thoughts (sometimes presented as quiet muttering) being inserted into narration or dialogue:


Here we see a tendency to seamlessly insert the internal narration of heroines within narration. It goes without saying that they are almost all cut from the rework: the thoughts of heroines become largely implied rather than stated. Now, again, I must stress that aesthetic rules are not beyond reproach and to be applied universally; I do not present this with the intention of saying 'and that's why any work which has narration for heroines interwoven into the text is bad.' Rather, in this specific case, we can see a marked improvement from its removal. Why is that?

I'm familiar with a quite remarkable novelist who has written hundreds of unpublished novels purely for his own entertainment. While others may ease themselves into sleep by reading for a few hours, this novelist eases himself into sleep by writing for hours. At one point he described his general process for writing and, while many of his insights were remarkable, the one which has stuck with me the most is his firm rule that he does not know what his characters are thinking at any given moment. He avoids phrases like "He thought about" or "He abruptly remembered" because he wants their internal world to be mysterious and something to think about.

Now, where he goes from here is quite high level, and beyond the scope of this post, but I'll try to convey the significance in a single paragraph. The idea is that thoughts can be seen as 'objective truth,' and the process of obfuscating these truths makes reading interactive; at any given moment, we choose to read certain lines with certain context, we connect contexts to reasons, our mind explains the contexts and reasons, etc. But none of it is definitive: objectively factual. Were we to read the novel again, years later, our minds will be inclined to focus on different contexts and different reasons and produce different explanations. We can forever wonder "What was this character thinking in this moment?" and delight ourselves eternally with different interpretations and contexts. One may say this is where the 'fun' of reading can be, sometimes even for the author re-reading their own work.

Where this applies to LiL is simple: in the modern day of 2025, we can re-read LiL over and over and constantly find new things, focus on new contexts, apply our own relations, etc. And this is possible because Selebus DOES NOT TELL US WHAT CHARACTERS ARE THINKING (as much, anymore). We look at LiL 0 and very frequently the mystique of characters, even Maya, get kind of neutered by these unwelcome looks into the characters mind. The kind of 'objective reality' is forced on us and is much less interesting than the alternative. In Neo LiL, we come across Maya looking at her phone here and ponder what she's thinking; in LiL 0, we're told she's wondering 'if this is all worth it,' and instantly the mystique of the shot is gone.

Again, this is not a hard iron rule. There are points in Neo LiL where the thoughts of characters are explored directly. The important thing is for the author to be conscious of what they are doing. To be aware of the detriments of revealing too much, and therefore to be aware enough to measure the pros and cons when taking the action. The important thing in the case of LiL is not necessarily that these moments were cut; the important thing is the work was improved by them being cut, and Selebus - at some point - gained enough sophistication as an author to notice this.

I might say this is one reason why there is a tendency for writers to not actually improve over the course of their careers. It is not as simple as "oh, my syntax has improved by composing many sentences," or, "oh, my gray matter is now more flexible when it comes to summoning forth words from the dark ether." Improving at writing means grasping and tackling extremely high-level concepts such as the formation of nebulous contexts and reasons in the mind of the reader as they tackle an opaque text. If someone is not familiar or comfortable with these concepts when they first pick up a pen, it is not entirely likely they will suddenly discover them midway through a novel. It is more likely that one who does not appreciate this to begin with will never understand. And it's not like most writers seek out educatory texts on these matters, I think; I'm familiar with authors starting out in workshops and getting feedback from editors, but it seems to me most kind of just skate by on raw intuition once they get their foot in the door, since, after all, that was enough to get their first work out there. (This is all speculation though. There's like a million writers in the world and I have read a fraction of them; why the writers I am familiar with do not tend to improve significantly cannot necessarily be extrapolated across the entire population).

Moving on, the next point is a rather interesting one: the general rising of Sensei's intellect.


Essentially, almost every time where in LiL 0 Sensei had some thought like "I wonder who she's talking about" or "I wonder what that's about" regarding something obvious, Neo LiL just flatly changes so Sensei correctly identifies the subject. This is a highly specific subject, but one interesting to analyze from a variety of angles.

First, though, I would like to decry the temptation to view it through a lens of 'competence porn' as the trope goes. Consistently one of the more laughable lenses with which to view LiL is that of a bildungsroman wannabe where Sensei just needs to follow the hero's journey and end up having grown into a stronger, wiser man; with no offense, the hardest I've laughed is reading one user describe how they could not wait for Sensei to power up like Simon from Gurren Lagann to 'save all the girls' in the end. The comedy of this very concept was depicted in a recent event where Sana hallucinates Sensei coming to rescue her for her delusions, though I would not read too deeply into that myself and use it as my own bludgeon to silence oppositional discourse.

Rather, what I mean to say is that we should not view Sensei suddenly growing more perceptive and intelligence here through the lens of 'sensei becoming more competent' and therefore a superior character. That is a tempting line of thought but not what I believe is most meaningful here. Rather, there are two main ways I want to look at this.

The first requires invoking something only tenuously related: Knox's ten commandments of detective fiction. The ninth rule is rather interesting, and I will quote it here:

The "sidekick" of the detective, the Watson, must not conceal from the reader any thoughts which pass through his mind: his intelligence must be slightly, but very slightly, below that of the average reader.
Click to expand...
Knox's decalogue, of course, is not meant itself to be rules universally applied across detective fiction, much less harem slice of life stories. However, from it we can glean an insight Mr. Knox had an entire century ago: that reading is often more pleasurable when the point of view character mirrors the reader in intelligence or close to it. There is a certain instinctive impulse of disbelief when a PoV character is imperceptive or slow to a questionable degree: in the case of the above, almost every single reader will consider it blindingly obvious that Rin is interested in Chika, and so will only roll their eyes when Sensei does not notice this himself.

And are they wrong to? If we consider why these original lines may have been written, it is not likely they came from a place of genuineness. What I would detect is a motivation to artificially fan intrigue and simplify the plot: delay addressing these subjects and try to bait the reader into being more interested by not confirming their suspicions. These goals, of course, fell entirely flat if that was the idea; such imperceptiveness earns only ire and impatience, not intrigue, and so the text is only improved by their removal.

The second angle is simply that stories tend to be more interesting when characters are depicted in a more reasonable and realistic way (which is to say INTERNALLY consistent, not like 'stories about hyper-active manic pixie dream girls are bad because they are unrealistic). Stories tend to develop in more interesting ways when the obvious is observed rather than ignored, and when characters act reasonably rather than arbitrarily stupidly. We can say that Sensei observing Rin's affection for Chika (among other things: this is one example among many others) and changing his course of action in according to this is more interesting than him playing dumb. In this case, the drama of the story is heightened and the intrigue increased because the events feel more 'on our level' and difficult to predict. (It also helps that matters like this are why I can safely recommend LiL even to individuals with IQs four standard deviations from the norm).

Anyway, that's five examples, so that should do for now. We have seen that by the time of the rework into Neo LiL, Selebus's writing had improved in a multitude of ways: his narration is tighter, richer with humor and intrigue, free of various beginner traps regarding how to depict scenes or thoughts, and so on. There is not a single scene not dramatically improved on the rework. And this comparison didn't even bother to touch on "chu~", which is of course the actual lowest moment of LiL and something I will spare Selebus from being reminded of yet again, except by mentioning it now and encouraging everyone to read it on the PC if they haven't to laugh.
