With a week to go to the next LiL update, there is no better time to make good on my promise to analyze the writing changes to Lessons in Love brought about by the rework done a couple of years ago. To begin this comparison I would like to begin with a bit of an superfluous lecture: it is my near-universal experience that writers simply do not improve over time despite the common intuition being that people will improve at their craft over time. It really, really doesm ake sense that the more one writes the better one would get at writing, and therefore that we can anticipate writers improving. In general, though, I have found that not to be the case whatsoever. Most common examples of this are actually, by my judgement, misunderstandings of a completely separate phenomenon: that our evaluation of media improves the more time we spend with it. This is to say, we will have a harsher evaluation of Volume 1 of a book as it introduces characters and brings us into the world than we will on Volume 10 of a book where we are fully integrated into the story and all the gears are turning. I think people will often mistake this momentum for an improvement in writing quality when, in reality, the writing has not changed, only their perception of it. (More shallowly, a lot of people are barely capable of analyzing/parsing prose itself, and tend to associate e.g. improved visuals and music with improved writing somehow, as if a scene looking and sounding better suddenly makes the writing better too).
As for the writing itself divorced of all other factors, well, I have almost universally seen that authors simply do not improve notably over time. A genius will tend to demonstrate their innate talent in the first work they ever produce, such that even after decades of reading their work one can comfortably enjoy their debut work: Goethe stepped into fiction with The Sorrows of Young Werther and began composing Faust Part One in 1772 (see: the Urfaust); Gene Wolfe produced The Fifth Head of fucking Cerberus in 1972 and proceeded in swift order to release the Book of the New Sun, widely regarded as the greatest work of modern science fiction; I need not mention Tolkien; Dostoevsky began his rich career with the widely lauded Poor Folk; etc. Inversely, someone who produces shitty early work will probably never improve all that much (and I will spare the flame war which may arise by my listing of examples of poor authors).
In every case where I have read a series and felt that the writing quality has improved significantly, I've checked the credits and found that in reality a new writer was hired or something of the like. Every time I've followed an author for a long time, I've found their quality to be fairly stable with the usual peaks and valleys of chance resonance; even following long-term fantasy series, for example, I rarely judge that an author has improved after the 3 millionth word of prose despite the fact you would really expect that much quantity to have made a difference. And yet, it almost never does; a good author may may get a bit better, but a shitty author or mediocre author almost never raise to greatness. Of course, I am but one man and I have certainly not read every single author to ever live, so I can speak only of a trend as I see it.
This now brings us to Lessons in Love: a very rare (in my experience) exception to this. Selebus did in fact improve as an author, and somewhat dramatically; I find this pretty remarkable and believe that this transformation would be well-worth studying for any would-be writer who finds themselves insecure about their prose. We can use Selebus's modifications of his own writing in the past to glean insights into what techniques are more successful than others. For the purpose of this comparison I will be using a copy of 0.23 that I grabbed from I believe the subscribestar, since it was the last version before the rework. For convenience I shall distinguish them as "LiL 0" and "Neo LiL."
However, before I begin, I must make one more superfluous aside: despite being rich with insight itself, I will take the liberty of skipping the opening of LiL 0. It is by far Selebus's greatest embarrassment and I would not like to shine a spotlight on it specifically after he took such great pains to purge it from the game. That's not to say that this entire endeavor of mine is not similarly a slap to the rework's face, but for dramatic effect I will skip the opening regardless; my malice is not so limitless.
Okay, and without further ado, let us finally begin!
An early example of improved writing would be in the first conversation with Ami, when Sensei forgets her name. (For the purposes of this comparison I will take what is stated at face value and not speculate on, e.g., the fact Ami is almost certainly not actually surprised Sensei doesn't remember her name.)
Spoiler:
Numero 壱
In the original Ami noticing this and introducing her name is a very bland exchange which completes the function of introducing her name swiftly but without much personality. In the rework, it occurs in a much more interesting way: first, "how can you just forget that we've been living together for years" is very natural exposition phrased as a question. Second, "what's next, are you going to tell me youve forgotten my name" plays into the dramatic irony that we the player know Sensei has forgotten her name and in fact her name is ??? as she states this. The pause as Sensei waffles on whether to be honest on this is an early insight into his personality, and then Ami's freakout afterwards is humorous (especially with the visual of her shocked face). To finish matters off with aplomb, Sensei says it's not personal - "probably," prompting another shocked reaction from Ami.
Now, I think the improvement in writing quality is pretty obvious, but since this is a rare subject to be discussed I will belabor the point a bit. The original is wholly unremarkable and almost entirely lacking in humor or character development: it's not actively bad in a way which will earn ire, but it also does nothing good, either, and there is no worse fate for writing than to be completely boring. The rework, however, excels in all areas and manages to tell like 4 jokes in rapid-fire succession. There's a rather popular video that contrasts the old Simpsons with modern Simpsons:
https://youtu.be/KqFNbCcyFkk?t=517
. The example used is how in Old Simpsons, a joke was never just a one-off; the jokes would have layers, and a funny sequence would build on itself 4-5 twists of expectations, instead of just being a joke and done. We can sort of apply this lens here; in LiL, the original text here... well... wasn't even trying to tell a joke, while the rewrite has humor exuding from every line.
Although I will be only providing a limited number of examples in this post, it's valuable to keep in mind that transformations like the above have taken place all over the narration of the original. Swathes of previously bland, "lazy" even narration is transformed into sequences of multi-layered and original humor. I simply can't cover each one (for example, how superior the introduction of the space war is).
But the improvements were not just in humor. Let us gaze up on example 2.
Spoiler:
Numero 弐
Again, most people with eyes will be able to distinguish the quality here, but I will belabor the point regardless.
It is here that I must invoke that most dreaded concept in writing criticism: show not tell. This is a concept INCREDIBLY misused by the populace at large and tends to be wielded like a club to criticize a work whenever a reader feels it is being boring in some way. The thing is that 'show' and 'tell' are vague enough words that one can apply them to almost anything: that is to say, someone can accuse anything they want to be 'telling' instead of 'showing' without leaving much room for argument. It is for this reason that 'show not tell' must be invoked with extreme care and a consideration for Chekhov's original purpose in bringing it.
And that purpose was to place greater emphasis on details rather than what the details are describing. Rather than say 'the moon is shining,' describe 'a glint of moonlight on broken glass' so that the reader can infer the moon is shining in a more evocative way. We can say (and this is of course my personal interpretation - there is no singular way of interpreting aesthetic rules in literature) that a reader will tend to feel greater satisfaction and immersion when they are putting many details together to form a whole in their mind rather than simply having the whole thrust into their face, and this Ami quote embodies this extremely well.
In LiL 0, despite how the scene seems to avoid a direct description, we are in reality clubbed over the head that Ami is disturbed by the question about her parents. A wordy, verbose passage descriptions all the various actions she takes, going to such extraordinary lengths as to describe her panicked breaths and wobbly knees. The moment is punctuated by a weak, "Um... Could you maybe ask something else instead?"
In this moment I would suggest there is zero drama or intrigue. We can feel the author telling us to be intrigued, telling us there is drama here... and because it is so obvious, we lose interest; there is nothing really for us to imagine or ponder. Ami herself becomes increasingly a bit of a pathetic figure as she weakly asks him to change his question. (again: not speculating as to whether this is all an act at this moment in time). The idea of alluding to Ami's trauma and the accident with her parents is clear, but executed extremely amateurly.
Neo LiL's superior execution is hardly a question. First, Ami cuts him off before he can even finish speaking, establishing her STRONG AURA. Second, she s simply says 'ask something else," giving no allusion to how she is feeling or what she is thinking behind her mask. When Sensei protests, she again cuts him off and demands he ask something else with no change in her smiling expression.
This is great. THIS is intrigue. We are being 'shown' the detail of her refusing to answer, and from this we start to paint the bigger picture in her mind. The initial characterization of Ami being kind of weak and lame was not strong, but already in Neo LiL one will be starting to sense Ami's latent psychopathy and the damage left by certain events. This dialogue is so good that Sensei (probably deliberately but maybe not) repeated it in a later scene with Wakana and Sensei, where Wakana references 'the jaws of life' and Sensei obstinately says "Choose another metaphor." This is how you get an audience intrigued in characters and wanting to learn more.
Another subtle detail is that he has universally excised bits of narration which imply significant passage of time. For example, the narration says she "focuses for a long time on the distant horizon," but this is completely dissonant with the act of reading the visual novel; we ourselves click through this line in matter of 1 second, and don't see any such deliberation from her, so immersion is hurt. It is a reflection of gained wisdom that Selebus knew to cut these out and in future narration pay greater effort to aligning the reading experience with the reality described in the text.
Now, I will take a brief aside to look at something which is not strictly prose but may be interesting to mention in part.
Spoiler:
Numero 参
In LiL 0, after looking at the book of students, the scene ends briskly and cuts to Ami in a bath. In Neo LiL, we find her leaning over Sensei's shoulder ominously. This isn't a matter of prose but in scenes like this we can see a matured ability to simulate the actions of characters and juggle multiple concepts at once; the scene goes from a simple "go to room -> look at journal -> put journal down" to a multifaceted "go to room -> look at journal -> Ami was there the whole time -> interaction between two characters" (blah blah). Macro improvements are less interesting in general though (since they're more obvious) so I'll leave it at that.
Anyway, moving on, let us look at the following examples of thoughts (sometimes presented as quiet muttering) being inserted into narration or dialogue:
Spoiler:
Numero 四
Here we see a tendency to seamlessly insert the internal narration of heroines within narration. It goes without saying that they are almost all cut from the rework: the thoughts of heroines become largely implied rather than stated. Now, again, I must stress that aesthetic rules are not beyond reproach and to be applied universally; I do not present this with the intention of saying 'and that's why any work which has narration for heroines interwoven into the text is bad.' Rather, in this specific case, we can see a marked improvement from its removal. Why is that?
I'm familiar with a quite remarkable novelist who has written hundreds of unpublished novels purely for his own entertainment. While others may ease themselves into sleep by reading for a few hours, this novelist eases himself into sleep by writing for hours. At one point he described his general process for writing and, while many of his insights were remarkable, the one which has stuck with me the most is his firm rule that he does not know what his characters are thinking at any given moment. He avoids phrases like "He thought about" or "He abruptly remembered" because he wants their internal world to be mysterious and something to think about.
Now, where he goes from here is quite high level, and beyond the scope of this post, but I'll try to convey the significance in a single paragraph. The idea is that thoughts can be seen as 'objective truth,' and the process of obfuscating these truths makes reading interactive; at any given moment, we choose to read certain lines with certain context, we connect contexts to reasons, our mind explains the contexts and reasons, etc. But none of it is definitive: objectively factual. Were we to read the novel again, years later, our minds will be inclined to focus on different contexts and different reasons and produce different explanations. We can forever wonder "What was this character thinking in this moment?" and delight ourselves eternally with different interpretations and contexts. One may say this is where the 'fun' of reading can be, sometimes even for the author re-reading their own work.
Where this applies to LiL is simple: in the modern day of 2025, we can re-read LiL over and over and constantly find new things, focus on new contexts, apply our own relations, etc. And this is possible because Selebus DOES NOT TELL US WHAT CHARACTERS ARE THINKING (as much, anymore). We look at LiL 0 and very frequently the mystique of characters, even Maya, get kind of neutered by these unwelcome looks into the characters mind. The kind of 'objective reality' is forced on us and is much less interesting than the alternative. In Neo LiL, we come across Maya looking at her phone here and ponder what she's thinking; in LiL 0, we're told she's wondering 'if this is all worth it,' and instantly the mystique of the shot is gone.
Again, this is not a hard iron rule. There are points in Neo LiL where the thoughts of characters are explored directly. The important thing is for the author to be conscious of what they are doing. To be aware of the detriments of revealing too much, and therefore to be aware enough to measure the pros and cons when taking the action. The important thing in the case of LiL is not necessarily that these moments were cut; the important thing is the work was improved by them being cut, and Selebus - at some point - gained enough sophistication as an author to notice this.
I might say this is one reason why there is a tendency for writers to not actually improve over the course of their careers. It is not as simple as "oh, my syntax has improved by composing many sentences," or, "oh, my gray matter is now more flexible when it comes to summoning forth words from the dark ether." Improving at writing means grasping and tackling extremely high-level concepts such as the formation of nebulous contexts and reasons in the mind of the reader as they tackle an opaque text. If someone is not familiar or comfortable with these concepts when they first pick up a pen, it is not entirely likely they will suddenly discover them  midway through a novel. It is more likely that one who does not appreciate this to begin with will never understand. And it's not like most writers seek out educatory texts on these matters, I think; I'm familiar with authors starting out in workshops and getting feedback from editors, but it seems to me most kind of just skate by on raw intuition once they get their foot in the door, since, after all, that was enough to get their first work out there. There's like a million writers in the world and I have read a fraction of them; why the writers I am familiar with do not tend to improve significantly cannot necessarily be extrapolated across the entire population).

Spoiler:
Numero 伍

LessonsInDissonance said:
This is an extremely uncharacteristic ill-placed assumption from you.
Akira is most definitely the centerpiece of a divine conflict, you don't know the details yet but from all we've seen there's no way someone can discard this possibility.
Click to expand...
There is context to what I said, which was regarding the parallel or lack there of between LiL and Fate/Stay Night.
Akira is most definitely not one of seven masters engaged in a proxy war by summoning servants to do their bidding. It is in this context that he's not a competitor in a (Holy grail) war, nor is Nao a Heroic Spirit in his service.

What has been suggested is that Nao-chan (TEMPLATE 9) was sent in order to help him/Kaori, but she follows another's bidding (or even her own) at the very least, not his. Akira's definitely also involved in a divine struggle, but there's too much uncertainty to call him even a centerpiece with certainty, much less a competitor.

Ultimately, my conclusion was in regard to the reference from Fate/Stay Night, invoked by Selebus, being either strictly aesthetic (which is my conclusion) or not. Anything beyond that is not what I was trying to argue.
SlidingSubject said:
Wasn't this directly contradicted in one of the happy events, I forget which?
Click to expand...
Antosha said:
Because Io is, first and foremost, intensely private. And doesn’t want to give Nodoka the satisfaction of thinking she knows anything about Io. And Nodoka CAN’T let that stand. So she keeps coming back back at Io until she finally guesses something horrendous that happens to be true—that happens to be Io’s most fundamental trauma (which no one—Nodoka included—has any idea about).

So Moonflare, I’m going to respectfully disagree with you here: Io may have been fighting back in her inimitable abrasive manner, but what Nodoka did was pure, stupid cruelty.
Click to expand...
I didn't disagree with this though.
What I tried to point out was that Io was the one that instigated Nodoka's comeback by not being able to keep her mouth shut, which you also nicely point out about Nodoka being unable to control herself either. Io is a private person, yet it was Io that agreed to jump on that competition, she could have refused. It wasn't Nodoka that put her there, and Nodoka until the point in which Io starts lashing out was strictly answering what the questions were.

Then Io starts being a dick about it, and Nodoka was an even bigger dick to her. I don't think anyone's gonna argue that what Nodoka did was reprehensible, but my whole point is that the replay generated a change in my perspective, because - at the time, one of the big discussions was about Nodoka premeditating the whole thing (based on her comment about it before the competition):
This time, however, I concluded that Nodoka was simply talking about her book, and that the foreshadowing comes from Selebus in regard to the theme of the event, rather than a mega plan from Nodoka herself.
Simply put, Io was feeling cornered from someone getting everything right about her and lashed out at Nodoka, which is a very dumb decision because Nodoka will strike back a hundred times worse. But it still is a different perspective between this being another piece of a masterplan that tries to break the world (as we once assumed), and just two girls being dicks to one another. Nodoka being worse obviously.

posts.content_html_raw:
Moonflare said:
There is context to what I said, which was regarding the parallel or lack there of between LiL and Fate/Stay Night.
Akira is most definitely not one of seven masters engaged in a proxy war by summoning servants to do their bidding. It is in this context that he's not a competitor in a (Holy grail) war, nor is Nao a Heroic Spirit in his service.

What has been suggested is that Nao-chan (TEMPLATE 9) was sent in order to help him/Kaori, but she follows another's bidding (or even her own) at the very least, not his. Akira's definitely also involved in a divine struggle, but there's too much uncertainty to call him even a centerpiece with certainty, much less a competitor.

Ultimately, my conclusion was in regard to the reference from Fate/Stay Night, invoked by Selebus, being either strictly aesthetic (which is my conclusion) or not. Anything beyond that is not what I was trying to argue.

View attachment 4475581

I didn't disagree with this though.
What I tried to point out was that Io was the one that instigated Nodoka's comeback by not being able to keep her mouth shut, which you also nicely point out about Nodoka being unable to control herself either. Io is a private person, yet it was Io that agreed to jump on that competition, she could have refused. It wasn't Nodoka that put her there, and Nodoka until the point in which Io starts lashing out was strictly answering what the questions were.

Then Io starts being a dick about it, and Nodoka was an even bigger dick to her. I don't think anyone's gonna argue that what Nodoka did was reprehensible, but my whole point is that the replay generated a change in my perspective, because - at the time, one of the big discussions was about Nodoka premeditating the whole thing (based on her comment about it before the competition):
View attachment 4475570
This time, however, I concluded that Nodoka was simply talking about her book, and that the foreshadowing comes from Selebus in regard to the theme of the event, rather than a mega plan from Nodoka herself.
Simply put, Io was feeling cornered from someone getting everything right about her and lashed out at Nodoka, which is a very dumb decision because Nodoka will strike back a hundred times worse. But it still is a different perspective between this being another piece of a masterplan that tries to break the world (as we once assumed), and just two girls being dicks to one another. Nodoka being worse obviously.
Click to expand...
Fair.

I guess my sense — even in the moment — was that Io was being a bit of a dick (whose motivations made sense, even not knowing what she was hiding, and who I kinda sympathized with), but Nodoka was being a huge, throbbing, veiny, dripping putz, shoving itself dry into any hole it could find, not caring in the least whether it fit—and doing it for no reason whatsoever aside from self-gratification.

I never really saw Nodoka as a master plan kind of person, though she loved to present herself as such. I saw her as manic and delusional, with occasional flashes of real insight. And we learned in subsequent events (some of) the origin and import of those flashes.

- "She was killed by Aliens a few years ago."

It seems to be kind of a coping mechanism thingy for what actually happens:
Yuu Narrator - "Hahah, just kidding."
- "She died of cancer."

Possibly the same when it comes to Saki's family (Presumably Sensei's mother's side of the family), who were just murdered:
Yuu Narrator - "Two years ago, she came home from school and found out that her entire family had been butchered by one of the neighbors."

- "His name is Franklin."
- "I won it for her at a festival two years ago."
Tsukasa - "And the whale is named Franklin!"
(Chapter 4 Tsukasa 'Vow of Silence' Event)
And the significance of Whales in general, considering how often they come up. (Tsuneyo, Sensei, Amy, Kaori and Ami in 'Il Cervo', etc have mentioned them)

I somewhat think that Sensei has conflated Saki and Sekai in his mind due to his conflicting feelings and memories, which has led to some decrepancies in lore, but that's just a theory.

----
Also, since I apparently can't help myself:
Antosha said:
Here’s what I took from Io going after Nodoka
Io actually questions the one thing that Nodoka cares about: that Nodoka is smarter and knows more than everyone else—and that everyone else acknowledge that fact. Because Io is, first and foremost, intensely private. And doesn’t want to give Nodoka the satisfaction of thinking she knows anything about Io. And Nodoka CAN’T let that stand. So she keeps coming back back at Io until she finally guesses something horrendous that happens to be true—that happens to be Io’s most fundamental trauma (which no one—Nodoka included—has any idea about).

So Moonflare, I’m going to respectfully disagree with you here: Io may have been fighting back in her inimitable abrasive manner, but what Nodoka did was pure, stupid cruelty.


And sober or drunk, I completely agree that Nodoka is way worse than Kirin.

Kirin does what she does because she’s horny and, let’s face it, isn’t the sharpest tool in the shed.

Nodoka does what she does because she can.

(Which isn’t to say that I dint find her an interesting, compelling, occasionally amusing character. But girl’s a psychopath. That it took until the last reset for someone to kill her surprises me. )

ETA: I’ve been thinking about the old saying, “Never stick your dick in crazy.”

Its a lesson I learned the hard way.

Most of the cast are pretty nuts, tbh. Otoha’s the least neurotic I can think of. A number of the others are teetering on the edge of psychosis.

But as of the end of 0.46, there are three girls (and a ghost) I think definitely qualify: Nodoka, Chika, Ami, and of course Mama Crazy herself, Sekai.

spoilers.html:
Yuu's mother/Presumably Sekai's and Sensei's grandmother, also was "killed by aliens":
Mom - "Yuu! You're going to be late for school!"
Yuu Narrator - "...Is what my mom would probably be saying right now if she could."
- "She was killed by Aliens a few years ago."

It seems to be kind of a coping mechanism thingy for what actually happens:
Yuu Narrator - "Hahah, just kidding."
- "She died of cancer."

Possibly the same when it comes to Saki's family (Presumably Sensei's mother's side of the family), who were just murdered:
Yuu Narrator - "Two years ago, she came home from school and found out that her entire family had been butchered by one of the neighbors."

Also, I still want to know how Tsukasa ended up with Saki's whale:
Yuu - "But you love Whales."
Yuu Narrator - "She has a huge stuffed whale that she keeps on her bed."
- "His name is Franklin."
- "I won it for her at a festival two years ago."
Tsukasa - "And the whale is named Franklin!"
(Chapter 4 Tsukasa 'Vow of Silence' Event)
And the significance of Whales in general, considering how often they come up. (Tsuneyo, Sensei, Amy, Kaori and Ami in 'Il Cervo', etc have mentioned them)

I somewhat think that Sensei has conflated Saki and Sekai in his mind due to his conflicting feelings and memories, which has led to some decrepancies in lore, but that's just a theory.

spoilers.html:
Io actually questions the one thing that Nodoka cares about: that Nodoka is smarter and knows more than everyone else—and that everyone else acknowledge that fact. Because Io is, first and foremost, intensely private. And doesn’t want to give Nodoka the satisfaction of thinking she knows anything about Io. And Nodoka CAN’T let that stand. So she keeps coming back back at Io until she finally guesses something horrendous that happens to be true—that happens to be Io’s most fundamental trauma (which no one—Nodoka included—has any idea about).

So Moonflare, I’m going to respectfully disagree with you here: Io may have been fighting back in her inimitable abrasive manner, but what Nodoka did was pure, stupid cruelty.

Are you seriously implying that a sexual assault helped Yumi to grew up? Nah, hell no. It totally changed her dynamics with everyone, yes. But I wouldn't say it is a good thing after all.
Click to expand...
I’m gonna use this as a segue to share my general feelings about Nodoka.

She is simply a natural disaster that is better to avoid than to confront. If you somehow managed to learn a positive lesson from an unpleasant encounter with her, you should thank your ability to learn, not her.
(I became a lot less bratty after breaking my leg during my early 20s, but I am not about praising any comminuted fracture anytime soon)

With all these being said, however, Matador was her one and only human moment and I am not letting anyone take that from her. No matter how all-time biased I am toward Yumi and no matter how out of proportion Nodoka’s revenge might be considered as, Nodoka had an understandable human incentive there, and that’s all we asked; she just failed to deliver a convincing one most of the time.

posts.content_html_raw:
Just finished CH3 finally and...wow. Just wow.

Tbh I had already spoiled myself that we were going to lose Maya somehow. Even then, through all the foreshadowing it should've been a pretty easy conclusion to come to.
I'm more in the mindset of not really caring about spoilers as much as most people because for one, I don't like surprises.
But mainly, it's the WAY that the story reaches the conclusion/reveal/whatever that holds the most significance to me.
I've always been deeply interested in storytelling as a medium and this story in particular has been continuously striking me in all the right places and surprising me...

How I originally thought CH3 would play out after learning she was going to be the crux was Maya somehow sacrificing herself to save Akira in some poetic, altruistic way. But I was NOT prepared for it to all happen so abrubtly and in such a roundabout manner.
It ended up fitting the story way more that she was able to get what she wanted before she went out, even at the cost of what's left of Akira's sanity.



Originally thought this was another instance of Akira tapping into his poetic side that seems to only come out when he's breaking apart. However, "By the Girl with Broken Wings" makes me want to think it was Maya this time, since a lot of the recent monologuing seems to foreshadow her end and in my mind this exerpt could potentially mirror her feelings atm.
Which is an interesting thought, because as far as I can remember she's not been shown to have any connection to poetry or literature thus far (feel free to correct me if I'm wrong.) But this makes me wonder if it maybe IS tied to her past in some way like it is for Akira/Sekai. Possibly Sekai influenced Akira who then influenced Maya in a sort of cycle of generational trauma/darkness and now she's sealed it away in her heart in a similar manner to himself.
Could her boxes be poems she's written perhaps??? I supposed that would be a bit too similar to Niki's storyline though...but man...it would kind of make sense. What else has she been doing to keep herself sane all these years? And even if it were cliche and redundant for her to have something written down to help herself or Akira remember her by when Niki already followed a similar beat, I could see it working if she just outright topped it entirely by having countless boxes full of poems/letters recounting her experiences...showcasing just how far she was willing to suffer for Akira's love.
Well, I'm sure Selebus has something even more unexpected in store for such a reveal tbh. If it's even something he plans on revealing in the first place, or maybe it's already been answered in CH4?



Reading Yggdrasil_Frahma 's recent post on the writing of LiL certainly got my brain moving, and it came back to my mind here. I think this is a beautiful example of what they were discussing as "the obfuscation of objective truth." Akira/narrator is constantly foreshadowing something being lost at the end of CH3, and he assumes (and by default, probably the reader as well) that he's going to lose HIMSELF by being reset instead of Maya. But we were CONSTANTLY shown that this is not the case throughout CH3. To me who has been spoiled and I'm sure those reading for the consecutive time, we can't help but see things in Maya's perspective and want to tie them to her. And things are left just vague enough to allow us that opportunity. Fantastic.



Why THIS girl in particular Akira? Why don't you feel scared of losing what you have with the other girls if YOU are going to be reset like you say you are.



And then he mentions the 3rd choice...he knows it's an option. He just doesn't wanna face it until it happens. In a way she DOES sacrifice herself to keep him going, but it's not in some heroic, selfless way. No, in fact it's the opposite. She can't hold herself back anymore after she tells him he loves her. And in a bizarre twist of fate, SHE is the one who ends up reset because of it, because she allows him into her.




Things get a little wacky here, but I assume this is the point the Apocalypse/Reset begins.




She knows. Man...beautiful how it ends up isn't it? Her MASK finally breaks and she takes what shes been holding herself from, and she knows that it's not him that's losing himself this time, it's her. Tragic and perfect. No words



SUNFLOWER??? Who IS Himawari?

BONUS but I've already used too many screenshots:
- Grown up Chinami in a porn video got a shock out of me. Felt like screaming "NOOOOOOOO" at the screen XD
- Ayane mentioning that others hear "voices" too is interesting and something to take note of...
- Still don't really know the significance of Rain King, but that was a trip
- Narrator chastising Akira for being so self-absorbed and actually believing the others were free from consequences and that the world revolved solely around him.

spoilers.html:
Tbh I had already spoiled myself that we were going to lose Maya somehow. Even then, through all the foreshadowing it should've been a pretty easy conclusion to come to.
I'm more in the mindset of not really caring about spoilers as much as most people because for one, I don't like surprises.
But mainly, it's the WAY that the story reaches the conclusion/reveal/whatever that holds the most significance to me.
I've always been deeply interested in storytelling as a medium and this story in particular has been continuously striking me in all the right places and surprising me...

How I originally thought CH3 would play out after learning she was going to be the crux was Maya somehow sacrificing herself to save Akira in some poetic, altruistic way. But I was NOT prepared for it to all happen so abrubtly and in such a roundabout manner.
It ended up fitting the story way more that she was able to get what she wanted before she went out, even at the cost of what's left of Akira's sanity.



Originally thought this was another instance of Akira tapping into his poetic side that seems to only come out when he's breaking apart. However, "By the Girl with Broken Wings" makes me want to think it was Maya this time, since a lot of the recent monologuing seems to foreshadow her end and in my mind this exerpt could potentially mirror her feelings atm.
Which is an interesting thought, because as far as I can remember she's not been shown to have any connection to poetry or literature thus far (feel free to correct me if I'm wrong.) But this makes me wonder if it maybe IS tied to her past in some way like it is for Akira/Sekai. Possibly Sekai influenced Akira who then influenced Maya in a sort of cycle of generational trauma/darkness and now she's sealed it away in her heart in a similar manner to himself.
Could her boxes be poems she's written perhaps??? I supposed that would be a bit too similar to Niki's storyline though...but man...it would kind of make sense. What else has she been doing to keep herself sane all these years? And even if it were cliche and redundant for her to have something written down to help herself or Akira remember her by when Niki already followed a similar beat, I could see it working if she just outright topped it entirely by having countless boxes full of poems/letters recounting her experiences...showcasing just how far she was willing to suffer for Akira's love.
Well, I'm sure Selebus has something even more unexpected in store for such a reveal tbh. If it's even something he plans on revealing in the first place, or maybe it's already been answered in CH4?

We can root for him to get better, but not support his current misdeeds. Being an accomplice to the crimes of those two should not be something the mc should want, yet he clings to it like a confused animal having it's parents killer giving it food for adoption. Obviously an excessive metaphor but the concept is right.

remember to smile, for if you don't- you get jumpscared?

spoilers.html:
Hmm? Did Maya or the world(God?) erase Ayane's memory of the boxes? Given how interesting those were even to Ayane, I can't even imagine what could be in there.

Damn dude, I guess Maya isn't used to being told to stop. Bet she wishes Ayane never appears on that rooftop that one day.

WOW DUDE! Just gonna go and assume a favor Wakana is asking related to estrogen means she wants you to fuck her girlfriend, huh?

So both Osako and Wakana are 28.

They can wear whatever they want? Did they loosen the dress code? Convenient.

Yumi finding out about the dress code changes then joking that Chika is gonna tell her about another thing that's gonna ruin her school life, which conveniently happens to be the mandatory club assignment.

I still don't understand how the richest family in Kumon-mi isn't allowed to come and go as they please.

remember to smile, for if you don't- you get jumpscared?

Ami reading Tsuneyo's mind. "Noodles."

Rin's whole vibe has changed because of that hairstyle. I think I think she's cuter but I'm not sure nor am I sure there is some other underlying emotion.
What I can say however is that she has now separated her haircut from resembling Chika's. Only a matter of time before it stops resembling Otoha's too which is a thing I think I know is going to happen.

I see two uncomfortable friends about to talk about something difficult caused by Molly's awkward approach to love. I still don't know how that talk is going to be or what it will be about beyond trying to repair the friendship.

And seriously, Rin is like a whole new person with that haircut and outfit... If Rin had a sister, that's probably how she would look.

No, Molly. It's worse to ignore someone's feelings than it is to not understand them. The former is a conscious decision to be cruel, the latter is no decision at all.

I don't think I would call Tsuneyo cool... Chill, maybe. But not the kind of cool that wears sunglasses, don't look at explosions and so on.

Oh, Molly noticed the shirt!

The mc forgot about being the manga club advisor. Completely forgot. Or the dev somehow forgot he had already put that in.

Damnit mc! You should have told Imani not to mention Wakana is the advisor for the archery club! This is such a typical mc slip up, like seriously. He really doesn't care at the end of the day.

Damn dude, Imani is savage to Makoto! "Page 1! section A! if your name is Makoto, shut up!"

Called it. Sana joining the music group.

Otoha worrying about a sort of love triangle situation? Can't really see any other reason since Sana was allowed to join with no experience with drums.

Damnit Io! It's one word!

Imani already knows how Nodoka works. Super genius who undresses people with her eyes and doesn't have the courage to make a move.

Yumi? Swim club? WHAT? Mighty brave choosing the swim club over archery. I guess it sort of IS the most fitting one for her since she doesn't do music, is probably not into weeb shit... wait, doesn't she have a manga closet of some sort... Even if that were the case, I imagine she wouldn't want to associate with other people like that and might find it embarrassing? And uhh, I guess archery might be too inactive and she probably has some excuse against it. Given how physically developed she is and likely strong, enjoying the beach, swimming fits. There is the concern about the mc visiting the them which you know he will and you know he will see Yumi and she will freak out about it, that is pretty obvious. Question is how badly she will freak out about it and if she will regret joining the club or if on account of being tsundere, she somehow hopes that will or don't mind it nearly as much. I dunno.

Yasu joining the manga club is definitely unusual but you know it somehow fits surprisingly well. Molly confuses her rants for games, Ami and Futaba are welcoming, Futaba is patient, Ami won't mind on account of Yasu not being into the mc (yet). Maya on the other hand... hmmm. Can an ultra believer like Yasu and someone like Maya who hates god but is involved in religious bullshit anyway get along? I don't think so. Which is why this could turn out funny.
Yasu is too weak for both swimming and archery and the music club's vibe is the opposite of hers... unless they went for some kind of baby metal religious rock sort of thing, but nah. By process of elimination, the manga club is the only one fitting for her. Oh yeah, also cosplay. She did participate in that gothic dressup.
Damn... It didn't take long for Maya to prove me right. She doesn't want this religious fanatic in the club at all. She also did just say she would rather read in the dorms. But her reason was because they keep calling her a nerd on the board...

Reaching freeroam sure took a while. And to think that 2 days ago I thought I could somehow get the pre-reset, happy event, reset and whatever comes after until freeroam done in just like 2 hours... Yeah, I went to sleep early, played the entire day, went to sleep late at 6 am and have felt the lack of energy today and I just now at 8:40 pm manages to reach freeroam. Crazy.

Oh, I unlocked more areas! Fun.
Oh that's a lot of potential interactions. If there's at least one unique repeatable dialogue, it could potentially be another 23 to see.

Had my first proper test at archery not so long ago. Proper draw-weights, some weight to the bow although I don't remember. Some training on how to stand and such. It's not as easy as it may seem even doing it indoors. Any micro movements can throw off the 5-10 meter away target precision by quite a bit, more than enough to miss a target. I would do that again if I had easy access to it. Used those handguard things and if you are not careful and hit your arm with the string, oof that will sting and you will feel it for a little while. Those strings are not to be messed with. They could probably be used a weapon by themselves if angles correctly and the opponent is dumb and slow enough.

Given how Yasu have expressed the ability of foresight, it's not too hard to believe that she knew he would show up on this day needing the remaining seat which was left unoccupied by the rabbits.

Yasu's already wide creepy smile gets even wider. Stop that.
And now what is that expression? This down the rabbit hole event doesn't help make Yasu seem like less of a religious fanatic.
She definitely has the ability to trigger these blackouts of his. If it weren't for the fact he has those, I might actually be freaked out by her sudden disappearance.

Ami's poor phone getting yeeted across the room... cat videos are dangerous.

Yasu has(had?) amnesia, probably.

I wonder what the percentage is of manga that lacks any physical violence, sex and physical romance that's popular enough for me to recognize? And I guess doesn't cover any topics that religion might not like.

It's weird that chapter 3 starts of with nothing but Yasu events after the first few main.

Have the owners come by declare the church abandoned and lock it up or something?

I really hope I'm not wrong about this but I can tell right now that that door is not opening for her again and that this is necessary for character development. She is far too invested in this religion of hers and I think whatever god like entity may or may not be watching over the world sees her destroying herself in delusions and forced this change to take place so that she will adapt to life and try to become a "normal" girl. If this is the direction Yasu's path is taking, I may get convinced to like this girl and admire her cute moments. Would an entire 10 chapters work if she was still obsessing over the church and her beliefs? I think I'm talking too soon but I think most of us can agree that it's hard to fall for a girl who pays more attention to her religion than the wonders of life in her delusions of some greater being. I doubt she will just forget about the religion, but she should at least slow down a bit and try to be a normal girl.

But really, if you were some god like entity and some girl wasted away her precious life dedicating it to you and you can't do much in return to her, what would you do? Would you let her continue in her delusions or try to push her to live a better life? This really is no different than spending like 6 hours on the computer to spending 12 hours. The former is a mild addiction that still allows you to live your life and the latter is a dangerous one(speaking from experience as you know). If there is some god out there, don't you think they would have tried to destroy my computer and have someone show up offering me a wonderful opportunity to get back into society? I think they would. Alas, I am not that fortunate but at least Yasu is.

Wonder if the reason Yasu's events are appearing first is to push her in the direction of falling in line with the other characters so the player can start to see her differently and she will be more open to participation knowing she can't spend time at the church the way she used to. Did anyone see this outcome coming with her being locked out of an abandoned church? I didn't, but in hindsight it makes sense.

Despite everything that's happened so far, I think the game has never told you that the things Yasu believes in are false. But I feel like locking the most religious character out of her place of worship in a game certainly speaks volume for her fake her religion really is. But I can't quite figure out why this god of her would stop communicating with her. Is that really something she has made up? I don't know how it all works. The door was locked causing Yasu's subconscious side make her conscious side believe that the god no longer speaks to her? Honestly, anything can happen with Yasu at this point.

Gosh her eyes as huge!

Well, you can still find her in the cathedral so it might not be closed for good. Or this is just some detail the dev didn't bother with. But he did bother with Yumi's broken phone which magically got repaired again.

I still don't understand how the richest family in Kumon-mi isn't allowed to come and go as they please.
remember to smile, for if you don't- you get jumpscared?
Ami reading Tsuneyo's mind. "Noodles."
Rin's whole vibe has changed because of that hairstyle. I think I think she's cuter but I'm not sure nor am I sure there is some other underlying emotion.
What I can say however is that she has now separated her haircut from resembling Chika's. Only a matter of time before it stops resembling Otoha's too which is a thing I think I know is going to happen.
I see two uncomfortable friends about to talk about something difficult caused by Molly's awkward approach to love. I still don't know how that talk is going to be or what it will be about beyond trying to repair the friendship.
And seriously, Rin is like a whole new person with that haircut and outfit... If Rin had a sister, that's probably how she would look.
No, Molly. It's worse to ignore someone's feelings than it is to not understand them. The former is a conscious decision to be cruel, the latter is no decision at all.
I don't think I would call Tsuneyo cool... Chill, maybe. But not the kind of cool that wears sunglasses, don't look at explosions and so on.
Oh, Molly noticed the shirt!
The mc forgot about being the manga club advisor. Completely forgot. Or the dev somehow forgot he had already put that in.
Damnit mc! You should have told Imani not to mention Wakana is the advisor for the archery club! This is such a typical mc slip up, like seriously. He really doesn't care at the end of the day.
Damn dude, Imani is savage to Makoto! "Page 1! section A! if your name is Makoto, shut up!"
Called it. Sana joining the music group.
Otoha worrying about a sort of love triangle situation? Can't really see any other reason since Sana was allowed to join with no experience with drums.
Damnit Io! It's one word!
Imani already knows how Nodoka works. Super genius who undresses people with her eyes and doesn't have the courage to make a move.
Yumi? Swim club? WHAT? Mighty brave choosing the swim club over archery. I guess it sort of IS the most fitting one for her since she doesn't do music, is probably not into weeb shit... wait, doesn't she have a manga closet of some sort... Even if that were the case, I imagine she wouldn't want to associate with other people like that and might find it embarrassing? And uhh, I guess archery might be too inactive and she probably has some excuse against it. Given how physically developed she is and likely strong, enjoying the beach, swimming fits. There is the concern about the mc visiting the them which you know he will and you know he will see Yumi and she will freak out about it, that is pretty obvious. Question is how badly she will freak out about it and if she will regret joining the club or if on account of being tsundere, she somehow hopes that will or don't mind it nearly as much. I dunno.
Yasu joining the manga club is definitely unusual but you know it somehow fits surprisingly well. Molly confuses her rants for games, Ami and Futaba are welcoming, Futaba is patient, Ami won't mind on account of Yasu not being into the mc (yet). Maya on the other hand... hmmm. Can an ultra believer like Yasu and someone like Maya who hates god but is involved in religious bullshit anyway get along? I don't think so. Which is why this could turn out funny.
Yasu is too weak for both swimming and archery and the music club's vibe is the opposite of hers... unless they went for some kind of baby metal religious rock sort of thing, but nah. By process of elimination, the manga club is the only one fitting for her. Oh yeah, also cosplay. She did participate in that gothic dressup.
Damn... It didn't take long for Maya to prove me right. She doesn't want this religious fanatic in the club at all. She also did just say she would rather read in the dorms. But her reason was because they keep calling her a nerd on the board...
Reaching freeroam sure took a while. And to think that 2 days ago I thought I could somehow get the pre-reset, happy event, reset and whatever comes after until freeroam done in just like 2 hours... Yeah, I went to sleep early, played the entire day, went to sleep late at 6 am and have felt the lack of energy today and I just now at 8:40 pm manages to reach freeroam. Crazy.
Oh, I unlocked more areas! Fun.
Oh that's a lot of potential interactions. If there's at least one unique repeatable dialogue, it could potentially be another 23 to see.
Had my first proper test at archery not so long ago. Proper draw-weights, some weight to the bow although I don't remember. Some training on how to stand and such. It's not as easy as it may seem even doing it indoors. Any micro movements can throw off the 5-10 meter away target precision by quite a bit, more than enough to miss a target. I would do that again if I had easy access to it. Used those handguard things and if you are not careful and hit your arm with the string, oof that will sting and you will feel it for a little while. Those strings are not to be messed with. They could probably be used a weapon by themselves if angles correctly and the opponent is dumb and slow enough.
Given how Yasu have expressed the ability of foresight, it's not too hard to believe that she knew he would show up on this day needing the remaining seat which was left unoccupied by the rabbits.
Yasu's already wide creepy smile gets even wider. Stop that.
And now what is that expression? This down the rabbit hole event doesn't help make Yasu seem like less of a religious fanatic.
She definitely has the ability to trigger these blackouts of his. If it weren't for the fact he has those, I might actually be freaked out by her sudden disappearance.
Ami's poor phone getting yeeted across the room... cat videos are dangerous.
Yasu has(had?) amnesia, probably.
I wonder what the percentage is of manga that lacks any physical violence, sex and physical romance that's popular enough for me to recognize? And I guess doesn't cover any topics that religion might not like.
It's weird that chapter 3 starts of with nothing but Yasu events after the first few main.
Have the owners come by declare the church abandoned and lock it up or something?
I really hope I'm not wrong about this but I can tell right now that that door is not opening for her again and that this is necessary for character development. She is far too invested in this religion of hers and I think whatever god like entity may or may not be watching over the world sees her destroying herself in delusions and forced this change to take place so that she will adapt to life and try to become a "normal" girl. If this is the direction Yasu's path is taking, I may get convinced to like this girl and admire her cute moments. Would an entire 10 chapters work if she was still obsessing over the church and her beliefs? I think I'm talking too soon but I think most of us can agree that it's hard to fall for a girl who pays more attention to her religion than the wonders of life in her delusions of some greater being. I doubt she will just forget about the religion, but she should at least slow down a bit and try to be a normal girl.
But really, if you were some god like entity and some girl wasted away her precious life dedicating it to you and you can't do much in return to her, what would you do? Would you let her continue in her delusions or try to push her to live a better life? This really is no different than spending like 6 hours on the computer to spending 12 hours. The former is a mild addiction that still allows you to live your life and the latter is a dangerous one(speaking from experience as you know). If there is some god out there, don't you think they would have tried to destroy my computer and have someone show up offering me a wonderful opportunity to get back into society? I think they would. Alas, I am not that fortunate but at least Yasu is.
Wonder if the reason Yasu's events are appearing first is to push her in the direction of falling in line with the other characters so the player can start to see her differently and she will be more open to participation knowing she can't spend time at the church the way she used to. Did anyone see this outcome coming with her being locked out of an abandoned church? I didn't, but in hindsight it makes sense.
Despite everything that's happened so far, I think the game has never told you that the things Yasu believes in are false. But I feel like locking the most religious character out of her place of worship in a game certainly speaks volume for her fake her religion really is. But I can't quite figure out why this god of her would stop communicating with her. Is that really something she has made up? I don't know how it all works. The door was locked causing Yasu's subconscious side make her conscious side believe that the god no longer speaks to her? Honestly, anything can happen with Yasu at this point.
Gosh her eyes as huge!
Well, you can still find her in the cathedral so it might not be closed for good. Or this is just some detail the dev didn't bother with. But he did bother with Yumi's broken phone which magically got repaired again.

spoilers.html:
Over the top insane Yasu, lets see how bad this is...
Does she have religion withdrawal syndrome or something? (I don't know if that's an actual thing but I imagine it is)
I'm kind of underwhelmed so far.
Yeah I can't translate that. Okay apparently it's because that's NOT caesar-cipher but rather Vigenère cipher with HOPE as the key, whatever that means.
The things she's saying and the fact her eyes are completely white makes it seem like she's no longer the one talking, but her god is.
...wtf? That translation is wild!
Welp, there it is. Game pretty much confirmed that god of hers took over.
Now if I were to decipher what is written there, basically her god considers her unworthy, is upset she's calling Him next to the one she's tasked with observing(aka Sensei), and then goes on a spiel about how she will only be loved by her god once Sensei cums inside her... I don't know what kind of religion this is but it sounds fucking insane(puns not intended).
This god of hers is horny af. No sugarcoating it's demands, just vulgar demands.

The god made her horny...
Like how the fuck can I tell if this is all Yasu pretending or if she really WAS possessed by her god and all this nonsense she talks is somewhat real?
And now they are both possessed. Is anything gonna happen? Will we get a scene with her this soon into the game? But the lust still says N/A. What does lust even mean in contexts like these?
This doesn't sound pleasant at all! Is this sex??? What do you call this?

Nodoka turning her room upside down. I have a feeling this is pretty normal for her. Doesn't make me less her any less, but if I found myself living with a person like this, I'm sure I would feel very differently.

She really DID go outside without pants. Are they at the abandoned school? There's also this song which could mean anything but positive.
This is fucking ridiculous. Adult teacher walking around with his prodigy teenage student in the middle of the night to an abandoned school while she's not wearing pants and is high on coffee and too little sleep. What a weird plot.
To add onto that. She is not digging a hole in the middle of that schoolyard in here state of madness.

I still don't understand the significance of triangle circle triangle.

Mystery girl sure likes to hang around this school. Is that the second or third time she's been here? Feels like the third time but I can't figure out when the first time was.
Mystery girl distracted him with threats of calling the police. Smart move...

How is that possible...? His outside the barrier? Then would Nodoka just get teleported back in?

Oh of course he would forget having met mystery girl before.

How very convenient. Non of that apparently happened at all... I feel kinda upset and disappointed.

Did I do things in the wrong order or is the game really wanting me to wait the entire week to do the next Nodoka event? God I hate when the game does this.

I feel like the designs behind Ayane and Touka were very much intended. Ayane's have blonde hair and blue eyes which I believe is suppose to be some sign of beauty or something. Given that at least blonde hair is on the lighter spectrum, you may naturally expect her to be more welcoming. Meanwhile Touka has black her which I guess is cut in a certain way to show some grace or something and she is less welcoming but not exactly hostile. She follows more traditional values and such and has arguably the best body, both based on the lore I know and visually so. So it's like her physical genes are suppose to match her social status and it would be strange if her hair wasn't black to show that she's a true Japanese traditionalist or something. I'm not making 100% sense of these "opposites" but I can sort of see it. Just like how Niki's hair is pink and she's an adult, which is probably the preferred solo idol color, at least in anime. But I'm basing that off nothing. Point is, all 3 are relatively rich and paints a very stereotypical vibe of sorts.

He is still taking out sex toys out of their boxes to mess with Makoto. Why does Makoto like him again?

Poor Molly! Getting cleaning liquid in her eyes because the mc decided to aim for her face. If you remove the "cleaning liquid" part of that comment, it would have a very different implication.

Nodoka going around groping everyone in the showers huh. She can probably get away with that perfectly fine given her intelligence.
Nodoka "knows" about Makoto's relationship with him. Not too surprising.
So close. Maybe next time.
Nodoka is like a better version of Makoto now that I think about it.
There are 5 Nodoka scenes yet to be unlocked. Wonder if this will continue with Sensei fucking all her friends while she watches or if she will stop being stubborn and try to get some of her own experiences to write about.
Yumi behind teaser, hmm...
Oh, OH! Okay! What a sight!
HAHAHAHAHAHA!!! Nodoka stole Yumi's clothes! I don't know what to say here, that's fucking hilarious! Serves her right for being so rude, huh? The delinquint part time bully gets bullied!

Holy fuck, Nodoka is devilish! I love it! Is she gonna try to traumatize Yumi by letting the mc see her in that condition?
I feel so bad for what's about to happen but I feel less bad about who it is.
Oh no! Okay, maybe I DO feel quite bad after all! This is Nodoka putting oil on the fire! Yumi is even crying having no idea what to do.
What I don't get is why she hasn't put on a towel or something (Nodoka took those as well). Those should be around and should cover everything, but I wonder if she has a new phone to call Chika with and if she could move around mostly undetected.
But holy shit, that body of hers! Is it better or worse than Touka's? I had to look it up in koikatsu. Apparently the only difference appears to be that Touka's breasts are just a tiny bit larger. Hmm...

Well, Nodoka and Kirin now have something else in common. The only difference is that Kirin punishes good people while Nodoka punishes bad.
Yumi's got a point. The mc is not a victim, SHE is. She had to deal with her clothes being stolen, crying and distressed and being looked at by someone who forced himself on her in the past. He on the other hand were deceived and got to look at Yumi naked which, lets be honest, is pretty fucking sweet given how attractive she is.
Nodoka deserves detension for tihs, and not the good kind. Is the mc gonna be responsible enough to do that on Yumi's behalf?

Even the mc acknolaged her beauty.

Nodoka that bitch! Now she's gone too far!
Why... I don't fucking understand... Why do the sex positive girls always have to go too far? If I was the mc in this situation I would have snatched her phone and threatened to smash it into a million pieces, then put her in detention. But I'm not the mc and this mc doesn't care enough to do something like that.

Threatening with blackmail now, unlike what she did with Makoto.
Of course it's revenge for Yumi bullying Futaba. And after Yumi went ahead and apologized to Futaba she STILL went through with this despicable plan.
Again, WHY, why do BOTH the characters who talks about sex so much have to resort to traumatizing others? FUCK DUDE! Of course it can't be that easy! One day ago Nodoka was heading to the top of the list and then she went and did something this evil knowing the mc won't do shit about it. She is willing to ruin Yumi's ONLY friendship after Yumi already went through hell and back just to get revenge! If the mc was smart here, he could threaten Nodoka with telling Futaba what Nodoka did. But of course, Futaba would be asking what he was doing with Yumi there and it all would go back to him trying to meet and fuck Nodoka. Fuck dude, I didn't expect Nodoka to use her smarts for something like this!

...I had a thought just now. If Nodoka wants something in return, hinted at wanting to see all her "friends" get fucked by the mc, then what's stopping her from making Yumi do something sexual with the mc right now?

Nodoka is the opposite of the mc... Mc hates seeing girls cry, Nodoka apparently loves it. She just had to be evil underneath all that sexuality...

Yep, there it is. She's asking Yumi to do something sexual.
What? So either Yumi pleasures herself in front of them to completion, or Nodoka pleasures the mc in front of Yumi? If Yumi chooses to pleasure herself here instead of letting Nodoka pleasure the mc, it means underneath that appearance of Yumi's, she likes the mc too much to let that happen.

That fucking smug look of Nodoka's... what's the answer?
I knew it! Is Nodoka really smart enough to think Yumi likes the mc?

I KNEW she was gonna use that excuse! She went for the masturbation option and then proceeded to say she is only doing it for Chika's sake but that's not true!
And I just remembered, both Nodoka and Kirin went for the trauma route because they wanted revenge for something that happened a while ago. In Kirin's case it was a competition she couldn't win and in Nodoka's case it's on her friend's behalf. God, I wish I knew how Futaba would react knowing what Nodoka did.

Welp. That's a scene right there.

Why did I not think of that? Could Yumi's words have caused Futaba to force herself to puke to go down in weight?

Man, this is painful... If you were presented with opportunities to hurt someone in order for them to grow to be a better person, you have to set aside your morals and look at it objectively. Nodoka is doing this out of revenge and she is smart enough to pull it off. I just wish one of the characters I liked wouldn't go to this length. I don't know how it would have been done, but if it was Kirin doing this to Yumi... I dunno, I guess I would have felt better knowing I don't have to see what Nodoka is truly capable of doing.

Nodoka is giving me a cruel lesson with this speech and I don't like it... Feel utterly helpless as a reader too. The game really is a test. Honestly at this point, I wouldn't be surprised if the game was preparing me for an inevitable rape ntr scene... I guess if I can handle that and I finish the game some 6 years laters, barely reacting to that content, it will just make me wonder, did the game break me? Or did it strengthen me?

Oh that would have been great! What y'all think? Would Yumi have chosen to suck him off instead of letting Nodoka do it if Yumi couldn't finish?

He was way too quick to let Nodoka come up for air there. Why does she have to be the only one who doesn't suffer, huh? WHY? Let her fucking choke on the thing, pass out! It's not like she stated in the rule that she has to be conscious while he has her finish him off!
Ruined orgasm...

Gogo Yumi! Destroy her fucking phone! Apparently Nodoka isn't smart enough to know what would happen right after the last picture was deleted.

In other news, Yumi's new outfit. I can't believe THIS is the debut of it.
Glad the mc is smart enough to realize his inaction really hurt Yumi. Never in a million years would I have expected this little "present" of Nodoka's to go this far... The dev could have chosen to end it there with him calling Chika and explaining Nodoka's prank, but that would have been far too happy for the kind of game I'm playing...
I imagine for another few chapters, I will keep wishing this game had a different mc. His far too cold. I thought chapter 3 was gonna change that, but chapter 3 has only just started.

At the end of the day, Yumi needs to learn to get along with people and Nodoka was the one who forced that change through trauma. I just wish the mc would have handled this situation better but I guess because he didn't, Yumi never got the justification and relief she needed. Meanwhile, Ayane never hurt a fly, yet she had to suffer for it. Kirin is objectively a worse person than Nodoka.

It speaks volume for how heartless the mc is when he says he doesn't know how he feels about Nodoka after all of this and Nodoka then take that to mean that his opinion of her hasn't changed. If you asked me that question? My opinion of her have changed quite drastically for the worse, but putting her in the same category as Kirin would not right. Kirin is a special kind of evil. Nodoka took revenge for herself because her friend who didn't want to take revenge had been bullied by Yumi for that long. Meanwhile, Kirin took revenge because she got second place in a competition BOO FUCKING HOO, big difference, not even comparable. That any of that make Nodoka some fucking hero? Not even close. But I'm sure that overtime she did everyone a favor and I will look back on this moment and backtrack on my answer.

The mc isn't doing a good enough job grinding affection with Yumi but I really hope this doesn't set them back too much.
Oh and also, that was TWO Nodoka scenes. Because apparently touching a friend's body and showing it off is enough to justify a scene. Meanwhile every other scene includes someone cumming. I don't agree with this, that's fucking bullshit.

Can someone remind me what my reaction was to seeing that Touka only has one scene in the game right now because I want to do that again but with Yumi, FUCK MY LIFE! One fucking scene with Yumi, that's it? I feel that creeping urge to smash something right now. Oh and I remembered now. AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA! Yeah, it went something like that.
Two of the most attractive characters with nearly identical bodies, both only having 1 scene. Does the dev hate us? I think the dev hates us.

I feel mentally exhausted. I want to go to bed, but it's a little too early and I don't know if I could sleep anyway. I would like to say it's not nearly as bad as I make it sound but I don't know what the game could pull that would put me in that bad of a move anyway.

From Yasu in the morning to misc stuff to a shit ton of Yumi and Nodoka stuff to back to a... frowning Yasu? That's new. Has she ever frowned before without tears or crazy eyes? This looks like a genuine frown of sadness, but not the kind of crying sadness.

Now I got thoughts I need to push into the back of my mind... I got so discouraged by the realization that Yumi doesn't have more scenes and nor does Touka that I just kinda felt... what if I stop playing here? Of course I'm not going to, but it's those kinds of thoughts that make me subconsciously zone out of boredom while playing, knowing there is very little to look forward to. Would it be entitled for me to say that the dev should have rushed in some new Touka or Yumi scenes in chapter 3 or early chapter 4 just to keep me motivated?

Yasu felt, Yumi spotted Nodoka, what is she about to do...?
Yuuuuuuup... Nodoka should have known better than to push Yumi this far. I genuinely hope Yumi doesn't get punished for this. The mc is the only one who knows the reason, but I doubt he has the balls to defend Yumi. If anything, he might be more likely to defend Nodoka.
Well, as it turns out, Yumi is NOT all talk after all. Which is surprisingly relieving.

Makoto: "I'm so disappointed in you, Yumi... it really seemed like you were getting better..." That triggered me so badly, I had the instant urge to smash my table just then.
Mc, you are greatly misunderstanding what you COULD have done! Fucking tell them that Nodoka did something to traumatize Yumi that she didn't deserve and say it's confidential! That's all you had to fucking done you absolute piece of shit! Fucking coward! I knew this piece of shit wasn't gonna do anything! Which is still better than actually helping Nodoka in this situation I feel, and I don't have to explain why.

GOD FUCKING DAMNIT MC! TALK! TAAAAALK!
I can't believe I haven't entertained the idea of wanting to punch this mc until now, fuck this mc FUCK HIM, stupid piece of shit!

Nodoka could have at least given the cryptic "I deserved that for what I did". But no, she feels the need to perv instead.

What's gonna happen to Makoto? Yasu? Hello?
Dafuq? What is Maki doing here and why does she look so... angry?
It's like all hell has broken loose... I still have absolutely no clue why Maki is that mad and why Makoto was called to the office. So many chain reactions these past 2 events...
So much anticipation...
I knew it... I had only one thing in my mind that would cause this. She was called to the office to be told that her father had past away... Maki was in that state fearing how Makoto would do when she found out.
I had another look at the main girls and I'm pretty sure Makoto is the only one with a dad in space who had to go to space while he was still present in her life. Given how much Makoto misses her dad... well. This is an emotional rollercoaster today.

Let me guess. The messenger that let them know Makoto's dad is dead also let Haruka know that her husband is dead?
Yep, phone call has only just started and it seems to just confirm my suspicion.
??? Never mind then.
Uhh, those eyes are scary as fuck.
Wait, don't tell me, he is back and found out about the relationship and left her?
Or maybe he didn't come back but she was told that his alive and fine so she can't hide behind the blanket that maybe he actually is dead and she's not a cheater.

I'm starting to see the pattern here. Crying, scared and concerned, angry, laughing. I've done all those things in the past couple hours.

Yuuup, there it is. Her husband is alive.

Honestly, waiting 2 months to hear about someone IN SPACE who died doesn't seem that weird considering that space is huge and they never said where in space they are. I imagine it can't be easy to hold phone calls with Earth from space and I imagine if they are gonna do that, they are probably gonna go through a long list all at once when the signal is strongest.
Also, time works differently in space than on Earth.
And yeah, an automated phone call... I think those might be easier to make from space on account of the delay.

Wait, how do Rin know Haruka and Sensei are going at it? I don't remember how she figured that out, or if it just happened.

I really don't care about Haruka... I really don't. I just get demotivated when her events pop up. And for this to happen NOW of all times after the whole Yumi and Nodoka situation.

Oh, greeeeeeat... And now they throw in a new character into the mix.
Pretty sure her daughter doesn't want her to visit because of her tattoos and Japan... they don't mix very well.

Maki is great at holding back, huh. Guess she's letting it all out now. She's fucking losing it...
Wow, dude. Slapping Haruka like that. Uncalled for.

Stranger in their house?

Why did I not notice that? Makoto eyes were the same as his own. They became that way after the jump too. Is it just depression or something else? A deeper understanding of the world maybe? Or get this, what if Makoto DID die and was respawned as someone else just like what happened to him?

Hmm, rape, blackmail and... fem dom? Think that's what this is.
Choking too.
I feel like this is gonna be how Maki discovers their relationship. If she walks in like I expect that is.

Oh... well that's just fantastic. Spent all that time going through chain events just for the game to finally throw me into freeplay with no Yumi or Nodoka in sight. Futaba is there tho but she's locked behind a Maki event which is locked behind a Makoto event which is locked behind Friday and right now it's Monday. Also there's an Io event but that one is also locked behind the Maki event and a Karin event and she has absolutely nothing to do with any of this. My point is... I'm exhausted and I wish the game wouldn't delay things like this when I had a fit of rage at the mc's incompetence.

What a fucked up day.
What a horrible fucked up day...
